security_advisory.summary: Mermaid configuration APIs allow prototype pollution
security_advisory.description:
### Summary

Mermaid's configuration setters (`mermaid.initialize`, `mermaidAPI.setConfig`, and `mermaidAPI.updateSiteConfig`) merge the caller-supplied configuration object into Mermaid's internal config using the `assignWithDepth` deep-merge helper that is vulnerable to prototype pollution.

Because these APIs are intended to receive **trusted** configuration supplied by the application integrating Mermaid, Mermaid assesses the practical risk as **low**. The vulnerability is only reachable if an application forwards attacker-controlled data directly into one of these configuration entry points, which is outside their documented usage.

security_advisory.summary: Mermaid Architecture diagrams are vulnerable to prototype pollution
security_advisory.description:
Rendering an untrusted `architecture-beta` diagram lets the diagram author write an arbitrary property with the value `horizontal` or `vertical` onto `Object.prototype`. A group id of `__proto__` is accepted as a valid parent.

### Impact

Any code in the same realm that reads a property of that name from an arbitrary object, or enumerates an object with bare `for...in`, observes the injected value (which can only be the string `horizontal` or `vertical`.

This may mean corrupted option/config defaults, bypassed truthiness checks, causing denial of service or logic corruption in the embedding application.

Because the injected value cannot be an object or function, this is not directly exploitable for remote code execution.

### PoC

```
architecture-beta
      group mermaidPrototypePollutionMarker(cloud)[Marker]
      service a(server)[A] in __proto__
      service b(server)[B] in mermaidPrototypePollutionMarker
      a:R -- L:b
```

releases.name: Ripple 0.2.0 — Unified Graph Workspace
releases.body:
# Ripple 0.2.0 — Unified Graph Workspace

## Overview

Ripple moves from a bounded sidebar preview to an independent Obsidian graph
workspace. Four distinct rendering modes consume one Vault index, relevance
filter and selection state. No upstream graph plugin needs to be installed.

## Highlights

- Immutable revisioned graph model and incremental metadata/link updates.
- Full workspace graph navigation, note opening and node inspection.
- Frontier, Dense, Cluster and actual 3D Galaxy views.
- Identical relevance eligibility and preserved selection across modes.
- Independent cameras, Frontier drag/pins and workspace-state restoration.
- Bounded opt-in local body indexing; no slider-triggered file reads.
- Self-contained production bundle, license inventory, reproducible build and
  cross-platform CI.

## View modes

Frontier uses a d3-force worker and Canvas navigation with draggable/pinnable
nodes. Dense uses a grid, batched points, viewport culling and label/edge LOD.
Cluster uses folder-seeded label propagation, visible convex hulls and
cross-community links; it is not Louvain or a crossing optimizer. Galaxy uses
Three.js, perspective xyz geometry, ray picking and OrbitControls, with a
deterministic spatial layout rather than 3D force simulation.

The modes share scoring and eligible nodes. Rendering budgets affect links,
labels and hulls only: Canvas modes draw up to 30,000 links and 120 labels;
Cluster draws up to 200 hulls; Galaxy draws up to 100,000 links, reduced to
5,000 above 10,000 visible nodes. Dense suppresses links below 0.3×.

## Compatibility

Real integration was exercised on Windows 11 with Obsidian API/app **1.14.5**
(desktop installer 1.13.7, Electron 43.3.0) in a newly created 32-note synthetic
vault and separate app profile. It covered loading, every mode, shared 65%
filtering, selection, real 3D rotation, independent cameras, note opening,
pins, themes, metadata updates, view restoration and plugin restart.

Other Obsidian versions, macOS/Linux host integration, mobile, other GPUs and
large real vaults are **NOT TESTED**. Linux/Windows CI and browser fixtures do
not substitute for those compatibility tests. Full evidence and synthetic
performance observations: [VALIDATION.md](../VALIDATION.md).

## Installation

Download main.js, manifest.json and styles.css into
`<vault>/<configDir>/plugins/ripple-graph-filter/`. Reload Obsidian, enable
**Ripple Graph Workspace**, then run **Open graph workspace**. Minimum app
version is 1.14.5. All runtime code, notices and worker source are bundled in
main.js; no extra asset chunks are required. Community directory submission
has not been made or approved.

## Known limitations

The index supports up to 50,000 Markdown nodes and resolved links. Body indexing
is limited to 32,768 characters/note and 8 million total. Attachments,
unresolved targets and Canvas cards are not indexed. Keyboard node lookup
lists the first 200 visible notes. Narrow the query for others.

Large software-WebGL context creation can be slow; synthetic 50,000-node runs
recorded long context-initialization stalls. Frame samples include outliers
and are not FPS promises. Active Frontier physics moves unpinned nodes and can
take time to settle. Unpinned positions are reseeded on reload; cameras and
pinned positions restore. There is no automatic bridge retention, 3D physics,
AI extraction, remote model service or automatic link writing.

## Privacy

Ripple initiates no network requests, telemetry or external service calls.
Indexes, body text, query and selection stay in memory. Mode, cameras and pins
are serialized by the official Workspace API. Original notes, frontmatter,
links, paths and other plugin settings are not written. Required runtime
libraries are bundled with their original MIT/ISC notices.

## Checksums

The Release includes [SHA256SUMS.txt](https://github.com/styayur/ripple/releases/download/0.2.0/SHA256SUMS.txt) covering main.js, manifest.json and
styles.css. Release assets are built from the final merged commit and compared
with CI bytes, then downloaded again and checked before delivery. The GitHub
Release body uses this document verbatim.

## Upgrade notes

The plugin ID remains ripple-graph-filter and the existing command/view IDs
are preserved. The display name is now Ripple Graph Workspace. Existing 0.1
leaves load the new view; move an old sidebar leaf into a main tab if desired.
There are no persisted 0.1 query/settings files to migrate. Four-plugin
discovery is no longer the primary UI: the modes are owned by Ripple and have
no runtime requirement for those plugins. Historical alpha assets/tags remain
unchanged.

releases.name: Ripple Graph Filter 0.1.0-alpha.1
releases.body:
# Ripple Graph Filter 0.1.0-alpha.1

This is an explicitly incomplete alpha for manual installation, not a stable
four-plugin compatibility release.

Ripple now provides an independent sidebar graph with local, explainable
keyword scoring, a monotone 0–100% threshold, live counts, fixed preview
coordinates, score details, and clear/restore. Empty queries restore the original
visibility. Optional note-body reads are bounded and local. The plugin never
writes notes, links, frontmatter or other plugins' files/settings.

## Adapter status

| Plugin | Source-audited version | Capability in this alpha |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GraphFrontier | 0.8.6 / graphfrontier | Read-only visible snapshots via documented api.runTool with listViews/getState/getGraph. External filtering/restoration unsupported: the upstream subset is shared and saved with layouts. |
| Advanced Graph View | 0.10.1 / graph-insight | Detection only; no documented safe external filtering API. |
| Smart Cluster Graph | 1.2.0 / smart-cluster-graph | Detection only; nodes, hidden state and pins are private. |
| Galaxy View | 0.6.1 / galaxy-view | Detection only; no stable documented controller API. |

No real Obsidian integration test was performed. Source inspection, upstream
fixtures, unit/Mock tests and browser SDK fixtures do not establish full live
compatibility. GraphPro is outside scope. Exact audited commits and minimal
upstream API proposals are in [ADAPTER_COMPATIBILITY.md](https://github.com/styayur/ripple/blob/main/docs/ADAPTER_COMPATIBILITY.md).

## Validation and limits

- 53 unit/Mock tests and 10 browser fixture checks passed.
- Formatting, lint, strict TypeScript, production esbuild, asset checks,
  locked dependency license audit and npm vulnerability audit passed.
- No known npm vulnerabilities at release audit time; no third-party runtime
  code is bundled. License: MPL-2.0.
- Linux/Windows CI, browser checks and build repeatability are release gates.
- Synthetic benchmarks include 50,000 nodes / 149,969 edges; they are core-only
  observations, not Obsidian UI performance claims.
- Desktop Obsidian 1.14.5+ only. Standalone indexing: 50,000 notes maximum;
  optional body index: 32,768 characters/note and 8 million total. Diagram:
  first 250 candidates / 600 links; list: first 100 visible results. Counts use
  all candidates. No AI, remote models or automatic bridge retention.

## Install

Download main.js, manifest.json and styles.css into
`<vault>/<configDir>/plugins/ripple-graph-filter/`, reload Obsidian and enable
Ripple Graph Filter. Open the graph filter command. SHA256SUMS.txt supplements
the required installation assets.

The tag matches manifest version exactly, without a v prefix. Current
[Obsidian directory rules](https://docs.obsidian.md/Plugins/Releasing/Submit%20your%20plugin)
accept numeric x.y.z versions; this alpha follows the requested prerelease
policy and is for manual installation. No community submission or approval is
claimed. A numeric stable release still needs safe upstream APIs and live
integration validation.

PRs: [#1](https://github.com/styayur/ripple/pull/1),
[#2](https://github.com/styayur/ripple/pull/2).

Release source: [`c4ff05431df0e8bd2889cabf6b10188d606a5714`](https://github.com/styayur/ripple/commit/c4ff05431df0e8bd2889cabf6b10188d606a5714).

# terics v0.6.0-rc.1

Release Candidate — 2026-11-06

## Highlights

- **URL-first Web intake**: drop or paste a university portal URL, identify the school/vendor/connector locally, then authenticate and extract through the extension.
- **Opaque extension handoff**: the URL contains no timetable payload. A one-time nonce, request ID, TTL, size limit, SHA-256 and Schema 2.0 validation protect the transfer.
- **Whole-course removal**: remove an entire semester course by exact `courseId` from JSON, ICS or a selected Google Calendar. Same-title courses, shared teachers, related overrides and non-terics events are protected.
- **UID migration**: dry-run legacy v0.1 UID mappings and apply only one-to-one matches after explicit confirmation.
- **XLSX hardening**: ZIP bomb, ZIP Slip, duplicate entry, encryption, sheet/row/column and XML-depth protections in both TypeScript and Python.
- **Google Calendar planning**: Create / Update / Skip / Conflict / Delete, target calendar display, legacy property compatibility, duplicate detection and manual-edit protection.

## Download

- `terics-web-v0.6.0-rc.1.zip` — static Web build
- `terics-extension-v0.6.0-rc.1.zip` — unpacked Chrome/Edge Manifest V3 extension
- `terics-python-v0.6.0-rc.1.zip` — Python 3.12+ Tkinter/Playwright source package
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` — SHA-256 checksums

## Web

<https://styayur.github.io/terics/>

The Web app remains local-first: no timetable upload and no backend proxy. Google direct sync is disabled unless `VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` is configured.

## Verified input formats

Automated fixtures verify content-based detection and parsing for:

- CSV / TSV course-list layouts
- HTML grid/list exports, including HTML `.xls` exports
- XLSX structured-column and week-grid layouts
- `.terics.json` Schema 2.0
- legacy ICS UID migration preview

Binary OLE `.xls` is not supported; save it as XLSX/CSV/HTML first.

## WHUT evidence

The WHUT Connector remains Verified only for the observed `2026-2027-1 student timetable layout`:

- 42/42 visible semester course blocks matched
- 13/13 period times matched
- 15 courses, 42 meetings, 242 weekly events
- first teaching Monday 2026-09-07
- Asia/Shanghai

v0.6 did not receive a new real WHUT login session in this environment, so this is carried forward baseline evidence, not a new v0.6 live acceptance.

## Known limitations / blocked gates

This is **not Stable**:

- Real Google OAuth authorization was unavailable.
- A dedicated Google test calendar was unavailable.

- Non-empty real `notArrangeList` / `practiceList` semantics remain unverified beyond synthetic fixtures.
- No dedicated WHUT adjustment endpoint is known.
- No signed Windows EXE and no extension-store listing are provided.

Do not treat mocks, synthetic fixtures or API HTTP 200 as real Calendar acceptance.
See `docs/v0.6.0-calendar-acceptance.md` and `docs/v0.6.0-legacy-debt.md` for the blocked gate record.

## Install extension

1. Download and extract `terics-extension-v0.6.0-rc.1.zip`.
2. Open `edge://extensions` or `chrome://extensions`.
3. Enable Developer mode.
4. Load the extracted directory.
5. Confirm permissions are only `activeTab`, `scripting`, `storage`.

```powershell
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m playwright install chromium
python main.pyw
```

## Problem and resulting behavior

Imperfect STEM queries previously reached the otherwise strong ConceptSession
pipeline unreliably: 42.27% exact concept sets, 39.58% first concept and 67.86%
negative rejection. This adds one deterministic offline Resolver v2 in TS and
Rust, with inspectable candidates/evidence and explicit ambiguity/abstention.
The ontology and provider indexes remain unchanged.

**Draft retained:** overall exact accuracy improves to 88.64%, but the 69.09%
holdout result remains 26.06 pp below development. Colloquial and formula-like
holdout accuracy is only 20%. This does not claim beta-level maturity.

## Resolver v2 implementation

- Mechanical NFKC, mathematical/Greek normalization and a reviewed script table;
  regionally different terminology uses full canonical labels. Deterministic
  idempotence tests include mathematical Greek Unicode variants.
- Separate 37-entry Query Lexicon with kind, language, confidence, provenance
  and rationale. Historical metadata stays outside ontology. Controlled Chinese
  question scaffolding is removed from unmatched text; area-scaling composition
  requires independently recognized linear/matrix context.
- Whole-token abbreviations with explicit FT ambiguity. A precomputed vocabulary
  generates bounded typo candidates on whole Latin words/phrases; short fragments
  cannot use generic correction. Adjacent transpositions are supported.
- Finite anchored symbolic/formula token patterns for vector operators,
  derivatives, determinant/eigenpairs, mechanics/ellipse/harmonic identities.
  No evaluation, runtime code generation, CAS or remote inference.
- Integer weights: canonical 100, ontology alias 96, lexicon 92, formula 90,
  symbolic/composition 88, abbreviation 86, typo 76. Acceptance ≥70, competing
  span margin ≥8, unexplained content −45. Longer compositions claim contained
  terms; independent requested concepts retain AND groups with OR equivalents.
- Search compatibility wrappers and ranked Universal Search share one resolver.
  Ambiguous concepts get localized keyboard-accessible choices; unknown queries
  preserve normal resource search. No automatic Workbench for weak evidence.
- Shared JSON feeds both languages; exact golden parity covers normalization,
  scores, groups, ranking, evidence and status. Input/depth/token bounds and
  runtime-fixture isolation are checked. Developer diagnostics are available via
  npm run debug:query.

Prepared version: 0.4.0-alpha.3. No Release is published. Full measurements,
holdout failures, mechanism/provenance overlap, performance, security, tests and
remaining limits follow.

  question scaffolding is removed from unmatched text; area-scaling composition
  requires independently recognized linear/matrix context.

  generates bounded typo candidates on whole Latin words/phrases; short fragments
  cannot use generic correction. Adjacent transpositions are supported.
- Finite anchored symbolic/formula token patterns for vector operators,
  derivatives, determinant/eigenpairs, mechanics/ellipse/harmonic identities.
  No evaluation, runtime code generation, CAS or remote inference.
- Integer weights: canonical 100, ontology alias 96, lexicon 92, formula 90,
  symbolic/composition 88, abbreviation 86, typo 76. Acceptance ≥70, competing
  span margin ≥8, unexplained content −45. Longer compositions claim contained
  terms; independent requested concepts retain AND groups with OR equivalents.
- Search compatibility wrappers and ranked Universal Search share one resolver.
  Ambiguous concepts get localized keyboard-accessible choices; unknown queries
  preserve normal resource search. No automatic Workbench for weak evidence.
- Shared JSON feeds both languages; exact golden parity covers normalization,
  scores, groups, ranking, evidence and status. Input/depth/token bounds and
  runtime-fixture isolation are checked. Developer diagnostics are available via
  npm run debug:query.

releases.name: Panostem v0.5.0-alpha.1
releases.body:
Panostem is a concept-driven STEM learning environment with native ManimGL authoring and rendering. This is an **alpha prerelease for Windows x64**, with a static Web player.

### What is included
- Ordinary multi-file Python projects, five templates, CodeMirror editing, optional canonical-concept metadata and typed scene parameters.
- Separate genuine ManimGL OpenGL preview, bounded task logs/history, line input, process-tree cancellation, MP4/GIF/transparent MOV rendering and PNG final frames.
- An explicitly installed private runtime: CPython 3.11.14 and 3b1b/manim v1.7.2 at `f427fc67df75513be0cd3f3329e327a9a19401c3`. The upstream tag's own package/banner reports 1.7.1. Sources and dependencies are pinned with hashes; project dependency installation requires separate consent.
- Versioned, SHA-256-checked local share ZIPs; static Web plays rendered media and displays optional source without executing Python. Exporting a ZIP does not upload it or create a permanent public URL.
- Existing concept search, learning Workbench, JSXGraph lessons, three locales, reduced-motion and external-resource boundaries are retained.

### Migration and installation
The repository is now [styayur/panostem](https://github.com/styayur/panostem). The public product/executable is Panostem. The desktop identifier `org.stemvisualexplorer.app`, SQLite data identity and existing `sve.*` browser keys remain unchanged. Older shortcuts/install entries may remain after the display-name change; do not remove the shared application-data folder. Historical tags/releases remain available. Actual HTTP checks confirm the old GitHub repository and historical Release URLs redirect to the new repository. The new Pages URL returns 200; the old `/stem-visual-explorer/` Pages path returns 404. A repository redirect does not redirect that static path; no unrelated repository, personal site or DNS was changed.

Use `panostem_0.5.0-alpha.1_x64-setup.exe` or fully extract `panostem_0.5.0-alpha.1_windows-x64.zip`. Check the complete file SHA-256 against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. WebView2 is required. Packages are unsigned. Python/ManimGL/FFmpeg are installed separately through Studio's managed-runtime action; the first setup needs network access and disk space. LaTeX/dvisvgm are optional user-selected tools.

The application remains **AGPL-3.0-only**. License inventories, copyright texts, immutable upstream provenance and separately governed FFmpeg/PyOpenGL notices are included. User scenes, media, textbooks and third-party assets retain their own rights.

### Verified scope and limits
Windows 11 x64 has actual native editing/rendering/preview/player tests, descendant cancellation and failure cleanup. Real 2D, 3D, physics and multi-file custom-updater examples rendered and decoded locally; Linux CI also rendered all five scenes with Xvfb/Mesa. Runtime contracts run on Windows, Linux and macOS; frontend, retained learning, Rust/Clippy, CodeForge and CodeQL checks are recorded on PR #33 and the release source.

Linux/macOS remain experimental and have no native release assets. The experimental Linux GTK/Tauri chain still resolves glib 0.18.5 with the existing VariantStrIter unsoundness advisory; Windows x64 does not link glib. Upstream-compatible remediation is required before official Linux support. Local Python runs with the user's filesystem/network permissions: a virtual environment or subprocess is **not an OS sandbox**. Experimental Windows Sandbox configuration export is implemented and contract-tested; the optional OS component is absent on the test host, so guest/GPU behavior is unverified. Optional LaTeX is untested locally. The preview console is line-oriented; IPython simple-prompt mode cannot install the Manim idle input hook, so continuous refresh at an embedded prompt is not guaranteed. Normal scenes use the native window loop. MOV playback depends on the codec. There is no generic pause/seek contract for arbitrary native scenes and no automatic updater.

Visual search for mathematics and physics — a lightweight, local-first desktop
client that searches several interactive STEM websites at once and shows every
result in one unified interface.

- Unified **mixed search** across 7 sources, queried concurrently in Rust with
  per-provider timeouts and isolated failures.
- **Deterministic relevance ranking** (no AI/LLM) and a bilingual

  WebView window with its own Back / Forward / Reload / Copy URL / Open externally /
  Pin / Close toolbar.
- **Workspace mode** — up to four results in a 1/2/3/4-pane grid, plus notes.
- Quick Look, inline/side preview modes, favorites, search history, dark mode,
  and a fully keyboard-driven UI.
- Small query syntax: `site:falstad wave`, `source:phet wave`,
  `type:interactive gradient`, `"standing wave"`.

### Sources

Math Insight · Falstad · PhET · BetterExplained · Physics Fundamentals ·
PhysicStuff · 猫田の物理

(PhysicStuff and 猫田の物理 are marked experimental.)

The attached `stem-visual-explorer_0.1.0_windows-x64.zip` contains a portable

next to the executable. Windows 10/11 with the Evergreen WebView2 runtime is
required (preinstalled on most systems).

- Some sites block embedded previews via `X-Frame-Options`/CSP; the preview pane
  always offers “Open in new window” / “Open in system browser” as fallbacks.
- Provider parsers are covered by fixture tests, but source sites may change their

security_advisory.summary: Unsoundness in `Iterator` and `DoubleEndedIterator` impls for `glib::VariantStrIter`
security_advisory.description:
The `VariantStrIter::impl_get` function (called internally by implementations of the `Iterator` and `DoubleEndedIterator` traits for this type) was unsound, resulting in undefined behaviour.

An immutable reference `&p` to a `*mut libc::c_char` pointer initialized to `NULL` was passed as an argument to a C function that that mutates the pointer behind `&p` in-place (i.e. as an out-argument), which was unsound. After changes in recent versions of the Rust compiler, these unsound writes through `&p` now seem to be completely disregarded when building the `glib` crate with optimizations.

This subsequently caused all calls of `VariantStrIter::impl_get` to violate the safety requirements of the `std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr` function - which requires its argument to be a valid pointer to a C-style string - resulting in crashes due to `NULL` pointer dereferences.

This was fixed by passing the out-argument pointer explitly as `&mut p` instead of `&p`.

This issue has been present since this code was initially added in `glib` v0.15.0. The mismatch in mutability was likely missed (and not raised as an error by the compiler) because the C function wrapped by `VariantStrIter::impl_get` is variadic (`glib_sys::g_variant_get_child`), and the pointer in question is one of the variadic arguments.

issues.body:
# [Major Roadmap] Rename to Whinset — A Less Ambiguous and More Seamless Windows Setup Experience

## Overview

I propose renaming Windows New PC Setup to **Whinset** and evolving it into a more coherent, predictable and user-friendly Windows provisioning tool.

The primary goal is to improve the PowerShell experience, eliminate ambiguous operations and reduce unnecessary interaction during system setup.

Whinset should make system configuration straightforward: users should understand the intended changes before downloading and running the tool, while the actual execution should remain as seamless as possible.

## 1. Project Renaming

Rename the project and its public-facing identity:

- Repository: `whinset`
- CLI identity: `whinset`
- Documentation and release assets should use the new name.
- Existing configuration and installation paths should be migrated or preserved compatibly.

Historical releases and existing user data must remain intact.

## 2. PowerShell Experience

Improve the command-line interface and eliminate ambiguous terminology.

Proposed command structure:

```powershell
whinset plan --profile developer
whinset apply --profile developer
whinset status
whinset doctor
```

The exact command interface can be refined during implementation.

Requirements:

- Consistent parameter naming.
- Explicit separation between planning and execution.
- Unambiguous package identifiers.
- Clear distinctions between skipped, unavailable, failed and completed operations.
- Structured execution results and exit codes.
- Idempotent operations where practical.
- Recoverable execution state.
- Useful PowerShell output without unnecessary verbosity.

## 3. Reduce Interaction During Execution

The execution experience should prioritize automation rather than repeatedly asking users to confirm individual operations.

Before downloading or installing Whinset, README and Release documentation must clearly explain:

- What the tool will install.
- What system settings it may modify.
- Which operations require elevated privileges.
- Potential consequences and compatibility considerations.
- Whether a restart may be required.
- What can and cannot be restored automatically.

Once the user initiates the declared setup operation, Whinset should execute the selected plan without unnecessary per-operation prompts.

Avoid introducing redundant confirmation dialogs for ordinary, already-declared installation and configuration steps.

## 4. Privilege and Permission Handling

Improve privilege handling to support seamless execution.

Requirements:

- Detect the privilege requirements of individual operations.
- Perform ordinary user-level operations without unnecessary elevation.
- Support elevated execution for operations that genuinely require administrator privileges.
- Minimize repeated elevation boundaries.
- Preserve a clear distinction between user-level and administrator-level execution contexts.
- Record the operations actually performed.
- Avoid silently weakening Windows security settings.

Where Windows requires administrator authorization, use its normal elevation mechanism.

The project should not rely on hidden UAC bypasses, credential collection or disabling UAC.

The intended experience is quiet execution after the required authorization, not concealed privilege escalation.

## 5. `beatwin.txt` — Copy-and-Paste Bootstrap

Introduce a lightweight `beatwin.txt` bootstrap instruction file.

Its purpose is to provide users with a simple copy-and-paste entry point for starting Whinset.

Requirements:

- Minimal and understandable instructions.
- Clear official download and source references.
- A predictable execution entry point.
- Support for the intended administrator bootstrap workflow.
- No hidden or obfuscated commands.
- No silent downloads or execution of unverified remote scripts.
- Explicit documentation of the permissions required.

The bootstrap should make installation convenient without obscuring what is being executed.

## 6. Execution and Recovery

Improve the reliability of system setup:

- Record operation IDs, targets and results.
- Preserve useful execution logs.
- Detect already-installed software.
- Handle interrupted installation.
- Distinguish reboot-required states.
- Provide diagnostic information.
- Avoid claiming rollback where an operation cannot actually be reversed.
- Preserve compatibility with existing Whinset predecessors' state directories.

## 7. Proposed Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Repository renamed to `whinset`.
- [ ] PowerShell CLI and naming conventions unified.
- [ ] Ambiguous operation and package selection behavior eliminated.
- [ ] Planning and execution workflows clearly separated.
- [ ] README and Release documentation explain all planned changes and consequences.
- [ ] Unnecessary interactive confirmations removed.
- [ ] Administrator privilege handling improved.
- [ ] `beatwin.txt` bootstrap workflow implemented.
- [ ] User-level and elevated execution contexts tested.
- [ ] Execution logging and recovery improved.
- [ ] Existing configuration and state migration tested.
- [ ] Windows 11 virtual-machine installation and reboot tests pass.
- [ ] Existing installation workflows remain compatible where promised.

## Scope Boundaries

The objective is not to build another Windows debloating or security-disabling utility.

Do not introduce hidden system modifications, undocumented privilege escalation, forced security-policy changes or unnecessary background services.

The intended experience is a transparent, predictable setup plan followed by seamless execution.

**Target milestone: Whinset v2.0.0**

releases.body:
# Whinset v2.0.0-rc.2

Release candidate only. Stable remains prohibited pending independent real Windows 11 acceptance. Roadmap Issue #8 remains open.

## Read before download

Whinset can install exact catalog packages, enable Windows features, update the machine WSL runtime, install Docker Desktop and change machine JAVA_HOME/PATH. Original-user work includes package/user environment configuration, WSL distribution registration and Docker daemon/hello-world verification. Installers may modify services, registry, startup entries, PATH and files beyond Whinset's state records. Review the plan and licenses before `apply -AcceptAgreements`.

Normal Windows UAC is required when elevated work remains. Different-user UAC credentials are unsupported and rejected. Start from the intended account and use same-user elevation. No credentials are collected and UAC is never bypassed. No automatic reboot or rollback is implemented. Restart-required work exits 3010 and waits for a manual reboot. State/logs remain under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Whinset\v2`.

## Changes since RC.1

- Original/elevated SID policy, private run ACL validation and state identity/operation checks.
- Native ERROR_CANCELLED (1223) classification; localized text no longer decides denial.
- Expiring requests, atomic single-use nonce claims, result nonce/run/hash/process-exit validation and stricter trusted graph reconstruction.
- Fixed the worker entrypoint to call its private function inside module scope.
- Separated machine WSL updates from original-user distribution registration, and Docker machine installation from original-user daemon/smoke checks.
- Rechecked interrupted installers before retry and successful packages during reconciliation; cleared reboot flags only after a boot-ID change.
- PowerShell remains the execution core. CMD remains official; Git Bash and Nushell are experimental forwarding adapters. UTF-8 JSON stdout and human-error stderr are tested across shells.
- Added security/recovery, shell, static-analysis, catalog/module, reproducibility and SHA-256 CI with machine-readable evidence. Added an actual disposable-runner package component install/recheck.

## Evidence and limits

Runtime evidence at `3d2af4ca538559d7023f8ed16a2dce17f614e9a2`:

- PowerShell 5.1 and 7 CI passed legacy, Whinset and hardening suites; the hardening suite has 19 deterministic checks on each host.
- Read-only CI shell tests passed for PowerShell 5.1/7, CMD and Git Bash. Nushell was unavailable in hosted CI; local Nushell 0.116.1 passed alongside the other shells (21 local checks including module validation).
- A fresh Notepad3 installation and repeated AlreadyInstalled verification actually passed on a disposable hosted Windows runner. This is package-component evidence, not Windows 11 CLI/UAC/reboot certification.
- Real UAC approval/denial, different-user credential rejection, clean Windows 11 multi-package apply, reboot continuation, WSL original-user first run, Docker first run/hello-world and vendor manual recovery are NOT RUN.

See `acceptance-matrix.json`, `docs/acceptance/windows-v2.0.0-rc.2.json` and `tests/VM-CHECKLIST.md`. PASS for deterministic orchestration does not certify the corresponding interactive test. BLOCKED means the required interactive environment is unavailable; it does not mean the test passed.

## Assets and recovery

`Whinset-v2.0.0-rc.2.zip`, `beatwin.txt` and `acceptance-matrix.json` are covered by `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The archive has fixed ZIP metadata and normalized text; rebuilding the same tree must yield the same SHA-256. The bootstrap pins only the RC.2 release URL/hash and defaults to plan mode. A draft asset URL becomes downloadable only after the RC.2 prerelease is published.

Published RC.1 tag/assets are preserved. RC.2 changes the plan identity; inspect old RC.1 state/logs and create a fresh RC.2 plan to reconcile installed packages. Do not rewrite an RC.1 plan hash to force recovery. Foreign-writable or inconsistent state is rejected for manual inspection. Request markers and atomic-write backups are retained as evidence. No automatic rollback is claimed.

Exit codes remain: 0 complete, 1 operation/worker failure, 2 input/agreement error, 3 compatibility cancellation, 4 UAC denied, 5 doctor unhealthy, 3010 restart required. Native/process diagnostics remain in structured logs.

releases.body:
# Whinset v2.0.0-rc.1

**Release candidate.** This is not the final v2.0.0 certification. Real clean-VM UAC, privileged installer, Windows feature and reboot-continuation acceptance remains pending.

## Read before download

Whinset can install software and make machine-level changes. Review this before running `beatwin.txt` or applying a plan.

- **Elevated operations may:** install machine-scoped packages, enable Windows optional features, install/update WSL and Ubuntu, install Docker Desktop, and set machine `JAVA_HOME`/`PATH`.
- **User operations may:** configure Git LFS, uv, Conda, Go, Rust and user PATH/environment values.
- **UAC:** `apply` requests one normal Windows UAC authorization when elevated work remains. All elevated operations are then grouped into one worker. UAC is never bypassed or disabled.
- **If UAC is denied:** the elevated phase does not start; status is `ElevationDenied` and exit code is 4.
- **Restart:** some installers/features can require a restart. Whinset exits 3010 and waits for a manual restart; it does not schedule or force one.
- **Rollback:** package uninstalls can be manual but are not guaranteed to restore every vendor registry/PATH/service change. Windows features, WSL distributions and Docker state require manual review. **No automatic rollback is claimed.**
- **Logs:** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Whinset\v2`. The bootstrap's temporary download folder is removed after the command, but permanent state/logs remain.

## What is new

- New canonical `whinset` PowerShell module/CLI and copy-paste `beatwin.txt` bootstrap.
- Schema 2 package catalog with exact Source:Id identities, vendors, architecture, scope, version policy, stage, privilege, dependencies, conflicts, expected state and recovery metadata.
- Exact stable-key/Source:Id resolution; display names are never install selectors.
- Deterministic dependency DAG planning with stable ordering, cycle/conflict validation and plan hashes.
- Separate plan and apply workflows with human and JSON output.
- One-UAC elevated worker; user-level configuration remains in the user process.
- Trusted plan reconstruction from the installed catalog instead of arbitrary elevated code.
- Resumable state, operation-level JSONL logs, reboot gates, package rechecks and exit 3010.
- Read-only discovery of legacy SetupNewPC state.
- PowerShell 7 primary support plus Windows PowerShell 5.1 regression coverage.
- Tab completion for commands, profiles, groups, stages and package keys.
- Deterministic release archive plus pinned SHA-256 bootstrap generation.

## Commands

```powershell
whinset plan -Profile Developer
whinset apply -Profile Minimal -AcceptAgreements
whinset status
whinset doctor
whinset resolve chrome
whinset recover -Retry
```

## Exit codes

`0` complete, `1` operation failure, `2` invalid input/agreement, `3` compatibility cancellation, `4` UAC denied, `5` doctor unhealthy, `3010` restart required.

## Known limitations

- Custom catalogs are plan-only in rc.1.
- The legacy WinUtil path remains available only through the legacy script and was not moved into the new elevated worker.
- Docker Desktop first-run setup and daemon startup can require manual action.
- Package inventory and installer behavior still depend on WinGet sources, Store policy, network access and vendor installers.
- Mocked tests cover orchestration, DAG ordering, UAC denial, already-elevated flow, resume and logging; they do not certify every real installer.
- Clean Windows 11 VM acceptance must be completed before publishing final v2.0.0. Current evidence is in `docs/acceptance/windows-v2.0.0-rc.1.md`.

## Verification

The release archive is built by `scripts/Build-Release.ps1`. `beatwin.txt` pins the `v2.0.0-rc.1` archive SHA-256 and is published both as a repository file and release asset. Compare it with `SHA256SUMS.txt` on the release page.

releases.name: WUTNet v1.5.0 — Windows hidden task recovery and PowerShell quality
releases.body:
# WUTNet v1.5.0 — Windows scheduled recovery and static analysis

Windows release, 2026-10-23. Android remains the separate experimental v1.4.0 artifact; this release contains no new APK. Historical releases, tags and assets remain unchanged.

## Changes

- `install` generates a managed UTF-16 VBS launcher under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\WHUT-Net`, dynamically resolves script/PowerShell/WSH paths, validates a harmless launch, then creates or updates **WHUT-Net AutoLogin**. `wscript.exe` hides PowerShell, waits and propagates its exit code. Task Hidden is only a Scheduler visibility setting.
- Five native triggers: current-user logon (5-second delay), NetworkProfile/Operational 10000 (3 seconds), current-user unlock (3 seconds), System Power-Troubleshooter 1 (3 seconds), and daily recurrence from local midnight with a two-minute interval and one-day duration every day.
- InteractiveToken, least privilege, IgnoreNew, a two-minute process limit, mutex, cooldown and backoff remain. Unknown networks are never automatically enrolled; authentication and credential protection are unchanged.
- Uninstall failures preserve config, DPAPI credential, logs, auto state and launcher; deletion follows successful task removal or confirmed absence. This includes the source fix absent from historical v1.4.0 assets.
- Approved `Stop-Whut` / `Initialize-WhutDataDirectory` helpers, targeted advanced-function interfaces and explicit command/parameter validation. Unsupported combinations return 50; public command names, JSON fields and existing exit meanings remain.
- PSScriptAnalyzer 1.23.0 development/CI gate, plus synthetic task/launcher regressions and safe local WSH/COM validation. No runtime analyzer dependency or Phase 3 WhatIf/Confirm feature.

## Download and upgrade

Assets: `whut-net.ps1`, identical `whut-net-v1.5.0.ps1`, and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Verify the exact filename's complete SHA-256, keep the script in its stable location, then explicitly rerun the new script's `install` to migrate an existing direct PowerShell/manual VBS task. Existing credentials and trusted networks are retained. If WSH/VBScript is missing or policy-blocked, resolve that with the system administrator; no policy is changed or visible-console fallback installed.

The tracked `whut-net-v1.4.0-fixed.ps1` remains a byte-identical source compatibility alias and reports 1.5.0; it is not the old published asset. The v1.4.0 tag and downloads retain their original bytes and behavior.

## Evidence and limits

See [field validation](../FIELD_VALIDATION.md) for dated authentication/reconnect observations and supplied historical hidden-window/unlock acceptance. New offline regressions and safe WSH exit-37/COM XML validation do not constitute real-device sleep-resume or periodic-retry acceptance. No real credentials, campus authentication or real task registration are used in automated checks. Windows Script Host/VBScript is required only for optional automation. WHUT still uses HTTP; DPAPI protects storage only. Android device authentication remains unverified.

Validation commands, analyzer exceptions and the CI matrix are documented in [Contributing](../../CONTRIBUTING.md). [Windows guide](../WINDOWS.md) contains the exact command matrix, trigger definitions and failure recovery procedure.

## 中文摘要

此版本仅更新 Windows：生成受管隐藏启动器并同步传回退出码，加入解锁、恢复与每日每两分钟重试触发器，保留互斥、冷却、退避、最低权限和可信网络限制；卸载失败保留全部本地状态。增加命令参数校验及固定版本静态分析门禁。下载脚本并核对 SHA-256 后，显式重跑 `install` 更新任务。Android 仍使用原实验版，旧标签和资产不变。历史现场验收、本次模拟回归与安全本地集成分开记录；未声称新版睡眠恢复或周期重试已完成现场验收。

## Delivery verification

Commit: [76393a2](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/commit/76393a209bf50787583b27524aef385723f573b1); merged [PR #7](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/pull/7).

66 offline cases pass on both PowerShell 7.2.24 and the current local engine. All 9 scripts parse and pass pinned PSScriptAnalyzer 1.23.0. Analyzer-rejection, WSH child-exit/false-zero and COM validation-only checks pass. Secret/history guard, architecture/50 local links and canonical/compatibility byte equality pass. No campus authentication or actual task registration performed. English/Chinese GFM previews pass at 1280px/390px.

CI: [PR Windows matrix](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/actions/runs/39907976933), [main Windows matrix](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/actions/runs/39908118858), [main architecture](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/actions/runs/39908118833). Historical field evidence is retained; new sleep-resume/periodic event delivery remains unverified on devices.

releases.body:
> Maintenance audit (2026-10-16): begin with `help` for offline, non-mutating inspection. `diagnose`/`status` do not send the password, but make network requests and may write logs/migrate configuration. The uninstaller currently catches Task Scheduler removal errors, deletes local state and can return 0 despite task-removal failure: verify the task separately and preserve needed private records before uninstalling. Removing state does not log out of the campus session. [Audit and blocked documentation PR](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/pull/5). Android remains experimental; release assets are unchanged.

---

# WUTNet v1.4.0

Windows 正式版，基于用户提供的 `whut-net-v1.4.0-fixed.ps1` 和开发日志收束；Android 同步升级为 1.4.0，仍为实验版。

## Windows

- 默认 `run`：已联网直接退出；已注册 WHUT 网络正常认证；新网络先验证协议，再请求一次明确的 Trust & Connect 确认。
- `trust-current -Label "WHUT-DORM"` 显式追加网络；`setup -AddNetwork` 兼容保留。WHUT-WLAN 与 WHUT-DORM 可同时登记，重复登记不复制条目、不改密码。
- `networks` 显示 ID、标签、物理指纹和登记/更新时记录的时间；`remove-network -NetworkId <id>` 删除单项。修复表格被 dispatcher 吞掉的问题，`-Json` 输出可直接解析。
- v2 单指纹配置自动原子迁移为 v3 `trustedNetworks[]`；v1.3.2 的 v3 条目自动补齐管理 ID/标签。账号和 DPAPI 密文保持不变。普通 setup 也保留旧注册。
- 自动模式仅接受完整匹配的前缀、网关、WHUT host 和接口类型；SSID/Profile Name/接口别名均不自动赋予信任。每次认证仍验证 WHUT bootstrap、config、CSRF、status，并在解密前重查物理网络。
- 发布整合保留 v1.3.2 的原子保存、严格 bootstrap IP/原始重定向路径、协议错误和 config.js 注释/大小写歧义检查。提供的现场修正版原件保留在本地 devlog；发布文件包含上述回归修正，并非原件字节副本。

## Android

- 版本 1.4.0 / versionCode 2，动态 `/api/r/<nasId>` bootstrap、多探针发现、同一 Cookie 会话和注释安全的 config 解析。
- 多个物理 Wi-Fi 指纹需在协议验证后逐个点击 Trust and connect 注册；系统自动入口只使用已注册网络，不读取 SSID。
- 保留 Wi-Fi Network 绑定、代理绕过、Keystore 存储及状态/联网双重复核；失败不回退到蜂窝网络。
- 发布 `wutnet-android-v1.4.0-debug.apk`，为可安装的开发签名测试包，不是生产签名发行包。不同签名的旧包需要卸载重装，凭据和信任列表会随之删除。

## 验证与边界

开发日志记录了 Windows 修正版列出旧指纹、显式追加 WHUT-DORM、保留两项注册和默认模式认证成功。最终整合文件通过离线回归；不将这些测试描述为一次新的现场认证。Android 已运行 JVM 测试、Lint 和 APK 构建，真实设备上的 WHUT 认证仍待验证。详细证据见 [现场记录](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/blob/v1.4.0/docs/FIELD_VALIDATION.md) 和 [Android 测试清单](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/blob/v1.4.0/docs/android-testing.md)。

## 下载与升级

Release 包含内容相同的 `whut-net-v1.4.0-fixed.ps1` / `whut-net.ps1`、Android debug APK 和 `SHA256SUMS.txt`。按校验清单核验文件。保留脚本固定位置；若任务原先指向其他路径，运行新脚本的 `install` 更新计划任务。

```powershell
.\whut-net-v1.4.0-fixed.ps1 networks
.\whut-net-v1.4.0-fixed.ps1 trust-current -Label "WHUT-DORM"
.\whut-net-v1.4.0-fixed.ps1
.\whut-net-v1.4.0-fixed.ps1 networks -Json
```

WHUT 当前使用 HTTP；DPAPI/Keystore 仅保护本地存储，物理和协议指纹不构成密码学服务器身份验证。

验证结果：Windows 47/47、Android JVM 38/38、Android Lint 与 debug APK 构建、APK 签名校验均通过。PR CI：[Windows](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/actions/runs/38131530013)、[Android](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/actions/runs/38131530017)、[文档](https://github.com/styayur/wutnet/actions/runs/38131530012)。

releases.name: WUTNet v1.3.2 — field-verified Windows captive-portal automation
releases.body:
# WUTNet v1.3.2 — field-verified Windows captive-portal automation

The first stable Windows release backed by reported end-to-end WHUT authentication and scheduled reconnect tests on Windows 11 with PowerShell 7.6.6 Core.

- Support the real `/api/r/<nasId>` bootstrap: validate it, replay it in the cookie jar, then open the canonical login page.
- Discover campus-specific `nasId`, `userip`, `acip` and `acname` dynamically across observed WHUT/BRAS environments.
- Select physical WLAN despite Meta/TUN routing; exclude APIPA/benchmark addresses and use the bootstrap user IP as an exact physical-interface hint.
- Parse active config.js API declarations without mistaking comments for assignments; deduplicate equal paths and reject distinct paths or unsafe API bases.
- Resolve the stable Microsoft Store PowerShell alias into a scalar Task Scheduler executable, with safe fallbacks and quoted script arguments.
- Preserve full success verification: login response, account-online confirmation and Internet recovery. Online `status`/`auto` and scheduled reconnect authentication are field-verified.
- Allow explicit registration of multiple physical networks with `setup -AddNetwork`. Config v3 uses `trustedNetworks[]`; existing v2 single-network configurations migrate automatically without changing the account or encrypted credential. Profile/SSID names never enroll a network.
- Retain DPAPI CurrentUser, late decryption, dedicated POST buffers, redacted errors, strict host/path checks and bounded multi-probe discovery.

## Usage

```powershell
.\whut-net.ps1 setup -Username <student-id>
.\whut-net.ps1 diagnose
.\whut-net.ps1 login
.\whut-net.ps1 install
```

Connect to another WHUT network and run `setup -AddNetwork` to retain both registrations. Normal `setup` resets the trust list to the current network. Re-run `install` after moving the script.

## Validation

The maintainer's field record covers real bootstrap, multiple campus environments, TUN coexistence, config/CSRF/cookies, credential login, account/Internet verification, idempotent auto, task installation and reconnect-triggered login without a browser. Multiple-registration enrollment/migration introduced during release preparation is covered by offline regression; no additional live multi-registration campus-switch test is claimed.

Release gates include PowerShell parsing, dependency-free offline regression, history/local-state secret checks, version/document consistency, clean Git state and CI. Assets are `whut-net.ps1` and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Limitations

WHUT currently uses HTTP; DPAPI protects credentials at rest only. Future portal schemas may change. Runtime/HTTP-stack copies cannot be guaranteed immediately erased. Fingerprints do not cryptographically authenticate the server. This release's client is Windows-only and requires PowerShell 7.2+ Core; Android is unchanged. No GUI, daemon, CAPTCHA solver, VPN manager or cloud service is added.

releases.name: WHUT-Net v0.1.0-alpha.1
releases.body:
Early, experimental public release of WHUT-Net for Windows 10/11.

- Single-file PowerShell 7 implementation (PowerShell 7.2+ Core).
- Zero third-party runtime dependencies.
- Dynamic WHUT captive-portal / nasId and API base-path discovery.
- CSRF + cookie-aware authentication.
- Windows DPAPI CurrentUser credential storage.
- Trusted portal and Windows network-profile checks.
- Proxy-independent local portal access.
- Optional Task Scheduler integration with dynamically resolved pwsh.exe.
- No resident process.
- Logs omit credentials, cookies, CSRF values, usernames, network-profile names, and raw portal response messages.

Validation: PowerShell Parser reported no syntax errors; help and command consistency checks passed; local synthetic checks covered portal/network trust, unsafe API paths, proxy bypass, cookie-session setup, and sanitised authentication rejection messages. GitHub recognises the standard MIT License (Copyright 2026 Stya Yur).

**The complete captive-login field test is still pending.** The unauthenticated WHUT session -> portal discovery -> authentication -> Internet recovery chain has not yet been fully verified against the live deployment. Task Scheduler execution after reboot/network reconnect also needs field validation. The upstream portal currently uses HTTP; DPAPI protects credentials at rest.

Download `whut-net.ps1` and optionally verify it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Credentials, config and local logs are excluded from the release.
